ahar vāvāsīn na rātrī /
sā yamī bhrātaraṃ mṛtaṃ nāmṛṣyata /
tāṃ yad apṛcchan yami karhi te bhrātāmṛtety adyety evābravīt /
te devā abruvann antardadhāmedaṃ rātrīṃ karavāmeti /
te rātrīm akurvan /
te rātryāṃ bhūtāyāṃ paśūn nāpaśyan /
sāven na vai paśyantīti /
sā na vyaucchad areklasyat paśuṣu /
tān devā icchantaḥ palyāyanta /
tāṃś chandobhir anvapaśyan /
tasmāc chandobhir naktam agnir upastheyaḥ
paśūnām anukhyātyai /
nāsmāt paśavas tirobhavanti /
sāved anu mākhyann iti /
sā vyaucchat /
te devā abruvann amā vai no vasvabhūd iti /
sāmāvasyā /
amā ha vā asya vasu bhavati
vindate 'nyasya vasu nāsyānyo vasu vindate ya evaṃ vidvān agnim upatiṣṭhate //
devā vā ahno rakṣāṃsi niraghnan /
tāni rātrīṃ prāviśan /
tāṃ devā na vyetum adhṛṣṇuvan /
ta indram abruvaṃs tvaṃ vai na ojiṣṭho 'si tvam imāṃ vīhīti /
stuta mety abravīn nāstuto vīryaṃ kartum arhāmīti /
te 'bruvann eṣa te 'gnir nediṣṭham eṣa tvā stautv iti /
tam agnir astaut /
sa stutaḥ sarvā mṛdhaḥ sarvāṇi rakṣāṃsy atarat /
indro yajamānaḥ /
yad agnim upatiṣṭhate
sarvā eva mṛdhaḥ sarvāṇi rakṣāṃi tarati /
nāsya naktaṃ rakṣāṃsīśate ya evaṃ veda /
tvaṣṭā vai bhūtvā prajāpatiḥ prajā asṛjata /
tvaṣṭā yajamānaḥ /
yad vai vācā vadati tad bhavati /
yadyad evaitad uddravati tattad bhavati tattat sṛjate //
meaning:
अहर् वावासीन् न रात्री /
सा यमी भ्रातरं मृतं नामृष्यत /
तां यद् अपृच्छन् यमि कर्हि ते भ्रातामृतेत्य् अद्येत्य् एवाब्रवीत् /
ते देवा अब्रुवन्न् अन्तर्दधामेदं रात्रीं करवामेति /
ते रात्रीम् अकुर्वन् /
ते रात्र्यां भूतायां पशून् नापश्यन् /
सावेन् न वै पश्यन्तीति /
सा न व्यौच्छद् अरेक्लस्यत् पशुषु /
तान् देवा इच्छन्तः पल्यायन्त /
तांश् छन्दोभिर् अन्वपश्यन् /
तस्माच् छन्दोभिर् नक्तम् अग्निर् उपस्थेयः
पशूनाम् अनुख्यात्यै /
नास्मात् पशवस् तिरोभवन्ति /
सावेद् अनु माख्यन्न् इति /
सा व्यौच्छत् /
ते देवा अब्रुवन्न् अमा वै नो वस्वभूद् इति /
सामावस्या /
अमा ह वा अस्य वसु भवति
विन्दते ऽन्यस्य वसु नास्यान्यो वसु विन्दते य एवं विद्वान् अग्निम् उपतिष्ठते //
देवा वा अह्नो रक्षांसि निरघ्नन् /
तानि रात्रीं प्राविशन् /
तां देवा न व्येतुम् अधृष्णुवन् /
त इन्द्रम् अब्रुवंस् त्वं वै न ओजिष्ठो ऽसि त्वम् इमां वीहीति /
स्तुत मेत्य् अब्रवीन् नास्तुतो वीर्यं कर्तुम् अर्हामीति /
ते ऽब्रुवन्न् एष ते ऽग्निर् नेदिष्ठम् एष त्वा स्तौत्व् इति /
तम् अग्निर् अस्तौत् /
स स्तुतः सर्वा मृधः सर्वाणि रक्षांस्य् अतरत् /
इन्द्रो यजमानः /
यद् अग्निम् उपतिष्ठते
सर्वा एव मृधः सर्वाणि रक्षांइ तरति /
नास्य नक्तं रक्षांसीशते य एवं वेद /
त्वष्टा वै भूत्वा प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत /
त्वष्टा यजमानः /
यद् वै वाचा वदति तद् भवति /
यद्यद् एवैतद् उद्द्रवति तत्तद् भवति तत्तत् सृजते //
text_mt:
There was only day, not night.
Yamī could not bear her dead brother.
When they asked her, “Yamī, when did your brother die?”, she just said, “Today.”
The gods said, “Let us veil this; let us make night.”
They made night.
Night having come to be, they did not see the cattle.
She realized, “Indeed, they do not see.”
She did not dawn; she clung fondly to the cattle.
Seeking them, the gods ran about.
They perceived them through the meters.
Therefore, one should attend upon the fire at night with the meters,
for the sighting of cattle.
Cattle do not disappear from him.
She realized, “They have sighted me.”
She dawned.
The gods said, “Our wealth has remained at home [amā].”
That is the new moon [amāvasyā].
Wealth remains at home for him;
he finds another's wealth, and another does not find his wealth, who, knowing thus, attends upon the fire.
The gods drove the demons away from the day.
They entered the night.
The gods did not dare to go through it.
They said to Indra, “You are indeed the strongest of us; go through this [night]!”
He said, “Praise me; unpraised, I cannot perform valor.”
They said, “This Agni is nearest to you; let him praise you.”
Agni praised him.
Praised, he overcame all battles, all demons.
The sacrificer is Indra.
In that he attends upon the fire,
he overcomes all battles, all demons.
Demons do not rule over him at night who knows thus.
Prajāpati, having become Tvaṣṭṛ, created creatures.
The sacrificer is Tvaṣṭṛ.
Whatever he speaks with speech, that comes to be.
Whatever he runs towards, that comes to be, that he creates.

iyaṃ pūṣā /

agne sahasrākṣa śatamūrdhañ chatateja iti /

agne gṛhapata iti

annaṃ me purīṣyājugupa ity odanapacanaṃ punar etyāpānyopatiṣṭhate /

tenaivānnaṃ guptam /
tad apānenātman dhatte //
meaning:
धनं मे शंस्य पाहीति /
आहवनीयो वै शंस्यः /
तस्मा एव धनं परिददाति प्रवत्स्यन् /
सो ऽस्य धनं प्रवसतो गोपायति /
मम नाम प्रथमं जातवेद इति
तन्वाव् एवैतेन विपरिदधाते विप्रवसन्तौ /
न ह प्रवसन्न् आर्तिम् आर्छति य एवं विद्वान् अग्निम् उपस्थाय प्रवसति /
प्रजां मे नर्य पाहीति /
गार्हपत्यो वै नर्यः /
तस्मा एव प्रजां परिददाति प्रवत्स्यन् /
सो ऽस्य प्रजां प्रवसतो गोपायति /
इमान् मे मित्रावरुणाव् इति /
अहोरात्रे वै मित्रावरुणौ /
इयं पूषा /
तेभ्य एव गृहान् परिददाति प्रवत्स्यन् /
ते ऽस्य गृहान् प्रवसतो गोपायन्ति /
अन्नं मे पुरीष्य पाहीति /
ओदनपचनो वै पुरीष्यः /
तस्मा एवान्नं परिददाति प्रवत्स्यन् /
सो ऽस्यान्नं प्रवसतो गोपायति /
धनं मे शंस्याजुगुप इत्य् आहवनीयं पुनर् एत्यापान्योपतिष्ठते /
आहवनीयो वै शंस्यः /
तेनैव धनं गुप्तम् /
तद् अपानेनात्मन् धत्ते /
मम च नाम तव च जातवेद इति
तन्वाव् एवैतेन व्याकरोत्य् आत्मनश् चाग्नेश् च यौ विप्रवसन्तौ विपरिदधाते /
अग्ने सहस्राक्ष शतमूर्धञ् छततेज इति /
सर्वेण वा एतौ तेजसा सर्वैः प्राणैः सर्वेणेन्द्रियेण व्यृध्येते विप्रवसन्तौ /
तान्य् एवैतेनात्मंश् चाग्नौ च दधाति /
प्रजां मे नर्याजुगुप इति गार्हपत्यं पुनर् एत्यापान्योपतिष्ठते /
गार्हपत्यो वै नर्यः /
तेनैव प्रजा गुप्ता /
ताम् अपानेनात्मन् धत्ते /
अग्ने गृहपत इति
शतं समा जीवतो नार्तिम् आर्छतः /
अन्नं मे पुरीष्याजुगुप इत्य् ओदनपचनं पुनर् एत्यापान्योपतिष्ठते /
ओदनपचनो वै पुरीष्यः /
तेनैवान्नं गुप्तम् /
तद् अपानेनात्मन् धत्ते //
text_mt:
[With the words:] “O praiseworthy one, protect my wealth,”
the Āhavanīya is indeed the praiseworthy one.
To him alone he entrusts his wealth when about to go on a journey.
He protects his wealth while he is journeying.
[With the verse:] “My name first, O Jātavedas...”
By this they exchange their two bodies while journeying away.
He who, knowing thus, goes on a journey after attending upon the fire does not meet with misfortune while journeying.
[With the words:] “O friend of men, protect my offspring,”
the Gārhapatya is indeed the friend of men.
To him alone he entrusts his offspring when about to go on a journey.
He protects his offspring while he is journeying.
[With the words:] “These of mine, O Mitra and Varuṇa...”
Day and night are Mitra and Varuṇa;
this [earth] is Pūṣan.
To them alone he entrusts his household when about to go on a journey.
They protect his household while he is journeying.
[With the words:] “O Purīṣya, protect my food,”
the porridge-cooking fire is indeed the Purīṣya.
To him alone he entrusts his food when about to go on a journey.
He protects his food while he is journeying.
Having returned, inhaling, he attends upon the Āhavanīya with: “O praiseworthy one, you have protected my wealth.”
The Āhavanīya is indeed the praiseworthy one.
By him alone is the wealth protected.
Through his out-breath, he places it in himself.
[With the words:] “Both my name and yours, O Jātavedas...”
By this he distinguishes the two bodies of himself and of Agni, which they had exchanged while journeying away.
[With the verse:] “O Agni of a thousand eyes, a hundred heads, a hundred splendors...”
With all splendor, all vital breaths, and all faculty do these two part while journeying away.
These he places in himself and in Agni by this.
Having returned, inhaling, he attends upon the Gārhapatya with: “O friend of men, you have protected my offspring.”
The Gārhapatya is indeed the friend of men.
By him alone is offspring protected.
Through his out-breath, he places it in himself.
[With the words:] “O Agni, lord of the house...”
Living for a hundred autumns, the two do not meet with misfortune.
Having returned, inhaling, he attends upon the porridge-cooking fire with: “O Purīṣya, you have protected my food.”
The porridge-cooking fire is indeed the Purīṣya.
By him alone is food protected.
Through his out-breath, he places it in himself.

yo no agniḥ pitaro hṛtsv antar amartyo martyāṃ āviveśa /
tam ātmani parigṛhṇīmahe vayaṃ maiṣo asmān avahāya parāgāt //
saṃ vaḥ sṛjāmi hṛdayaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ mano astu vaḥ /
saṃsṛṣṭās tanvaḥ santu vaḥ saṃsṛṣṭaḥ prāṇo astu vaḥ /
saṃ yā vaḥ priyās tanvaḥ saṃ priyā hṛdayāni vaḥ //
ātmā vo astu saṃpriyaḥ saṃpriyās tanvo mama //

meaning:
यो अश्वत्थः शमीगर्भ आरुरोह त्वय्य् अपि /
तं ते हरामि यज्ञियैः केतुभिः सह //
मयि गृह्णाम्य् अहम् अग्रे अग्निं रायस्पोषेण सह वर्चसेह देवाः /
मयि प्रजां मयि पुष्टिं दधामि मदेम शतहिमाः सुवीराः //
यो नो अग्निः पितरो हृत्स्व् अन्तर् अमर्त्यो मर्त्यां आविवेश /
तम् आत्मनि परिगृह्णीमहे वयं मैषो अस्मान् अवहाय परागात् //
सं वः सृजामि हृदयं संसृष्टं मनो अस्तु वः /
संसृष्टास् तन्वः सन्तु वः संसृष्टः प्राणो अस्तु वः /
सं या वः प्रियास् तन्वः सं प्रिया हृदयानि वः //
आत्मा वो अस्तु संप्रियः संप्रियास् तन्वो मम //
यत् पृथिव्या अनामृतं संबभूव त्वे सचा /
तद् अग्निर् अग्नये ददत् तस्मिन्न् आधीयताम् अयम् //
यद् अन्तरिक्षस्य यद् दिवो अनामृतं संबभूव त्वे सचा /
तद् अग्निर् अग्नये ददत् तस्मिन्न् आधीयताम् अयम् //
अग्ने गृहपते ऽहे बुध्न्य परिषद्य दिवः पृथिव्याः पर्य् अन्तरिक्षाल् लोकं विन्द यजमानाय पृथिव्या मूर्धन् सीद यज्ञिये लोके
यो नो अग्ने निष्ट्यो यो ऽनिष्ट्यो ऽभिदासतीदमहं तं त्वयाभिनिदधामि /
... यजमानाय पृथिव्या मूर्धन् सीद यज्ञिये लोके /
यो नो अग्ने निष्ट्यो यो ऽनिष्ट्यो ऽभिदासतीदम् अहं तं त्वयाभिनिदधामि //
समिधाग्निं दुवस्यत घृतैर् बोधयतातिथिम् /
आस्मिन् हव्या जुहोतन //
उद् अग्ने तव तद् घृताद् अर्ची सोचत आहुतम् /
निंसानं जुह्वो मुखे //
घृतेनाग्निः समिध्यते मधुप्रतीक आहुतः /
रोचमानो विभावसुः //
यास् ते शिवास् तन्वो जातवेदो या अन्तरिक्षे दिवि याः पृथिव्याम् /
ताभिः संभूय सगणः सजोषा हिरण्ययोनिर् वह हव्यम् अग्ने //
text_mt:
The aśvattha tree which, having the śamī in its womb, mounted upon you,
that I take for you together with the sacrificial banners.
In myself I take Agni first, together with increase of wealth, with luster here, O gods;
in myself I place offspring, in myself vigor; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, rich in heroic sons.
The immortal Agni who entered us mortals within our hearts, O fathers,
him we clasp in ourselves; may he not go away, having abandoned us.
I unite your heart; let your mind be united;
let your bodies be united; let your breath be united;
United are your dear bodies; united are your dear hearts;
let your self be dear to one another; dear to me be your bodies.
The non-mortal [substance] of the earth which came to be together in you,
giving that, Agni to Agni, let this one be placed in that.
The non-mortal [substance] of the atmosphere, of heaven, which came to be together in you,
giving that, Agni to Agni, let this one be placed in that.
O Agni, lord of the house, Ahi Budhnya, sitting in assembly, find a place for the sacrificer from heaven, from earth, from the atmosphere; sit on the head of the earth in the sacrificial place.
Whoever acts hostilely toward us, O Agni, whether a stranger or one of our own, here through you I cast him down.
... for the sacrificer; sit on the head of the earth in the sacrificial place.
Whoever acts hostilely toward us, O Agni, whether a stranger or one of our own, here through you I cast him down.
Serve Agni with kindling wood; awaken the guest with clarified butter;
upon him offer the oblations.
Upwards from the clarified butter shines your flame, O Agni, when offered,
kissing the mouth of the ladle.
Agni is kindled with clarified butter, honey-faced when an offering is made,
radiant, possessing shining wealth.
Those gracious bodies of yours, O Jātavedas, which are in the atmosphere, in heaven, which are on earth,
uniting with them, along with your troop, being in harmony, O golden-wombed one, convey the oblation, O Agni!

ojase balāya tvodyacche vṛṣṇe śuṣmāya /

meaning:
या वाजिन्न् अग्नेः प्रिया तनूः पशुषु पवमाना ताम् आवह / तया मा जिन्व /
या वाजिन्न् अग्नेः प्रिया तनूर् अप्सु पावका ताम् आवह / तया मा जिन्व /
या वाजिन्न् अग्नेः प्रिया तनूः सूर्ये शुक्रा शुचिमती ताम् आवह / तया मा जिन्व /
ओजसे बलाय त्वोद्यच्छे वृष्णे शुष्माय /
सपत्नतूरसि वृत्रतूः //
प्राचीम् अनु प्रदिशं प्रेहि विद्वान् अग्नेर् अग्ने पुरो अग्ने भवेह /
विश्वा आशा दीद्यद् विभाह्य् ऊर्जं नो धेहि द्विपदे चतुष्पदे //
नाको ऽसि ब्रध्नो ऽसि प्रतिष्ठा संक्रमणः //
सं त्वम् अग्ने दिव्येन ज्योतिषा भाहि सम् अन्तरिक्ष्येण सं पार्थिवेन /
वैश्वानर्या समिधा दीदिही न ऊर्जस्वत्या वर्चस्वत्या भास्वत्या रश्मिवत्या ज्योतिष्मत्या //

कल्पेतां द्यावापृथिवी कल्पन्ताम् आप ओषधयः /
कल्पन्ताम् अग्नयः पृथङ् मम ज्यैष्ठ्याय सव्रताः //
ये अग्नयः समनसः सचेतस ओषधीष्व् अप्सु प्रविष्टाः /
ते सम्राजम् अभिसंयन्तु सर्व ऊर्जं नो धत्त द्विपदे चतुष्पदे //

तस्यै स्वाहा /
या ते अग्ने पावका तनूर् अन्तरिक्षम् अन्वाविवेश या वाते या वामदेव्ये या त्रैष्टुभे छन्दसि या पञ्चदशे स्तोमे तां त एतद् अवरुन्धे /
तस्यै स्वाहा /
या ते अग्ने शुचिस् तनूर् दिवम् अन्वाविवेश या सूर्ये या बृहति या जागते छन्दसि या सप्तदशे स्तोमे तां त एतद् अवरुन्धे /
तस्यै स्वाहा //
text_mt:
O swift one, that dear body of Agni which purifies itself among cattle, bring that here; refresh me with it.
O swift one, that dear body of Agni which is a purifier in the waters, bring that here; refresh me with it.
O swift one, that dear body of Agni which is bright, possessing radiance in the sun, bring that here; refresh me with it.
I lift you up for power, for strength, for virile energy.
You are a slayer of rivals, a slayer of Vṛtra.
Go forth along the eastern direction, knowing; be in front of Agni, O Agni, here, O Agni.
Shining upon all regions, shine forth; bestow vigor upon our two-footed and four-footed [creatures].
You are the firmament, you are the reddish one, the support, the crossing over.
Shine, O Agni, together with divine light, together with atmospheric [light], together with earthly [light].
Shine for us with the Vaiśvānara kindling-stick, rich in vigor, rich in luster, rich in brightness, rich in rays, rich in light.
Those fires of the sky, those of the atmosphere, those of the earth that have come together, wearing nourishment and vigor,
having given wealth to this Agni, satisfied and pleased, go back home.
May heaven and earth be fit; may the waters and plants be fit;
May the fires, observing common vows, be fit individually for my supremacy.
Those fires which are of one mind, of harmonious thought, entered into the plants and waters,
let them all unite around the universal sovereign; bestow vigor upon our two-footed and four-footed [creatures].
That purifying body of yours, O Agni, which entered into the earth, which is in Agni, which is in the rathantara, which is in the gāyatrī meter, which is in the trivṛt stoma, that of yours I win through this.
Svāhā to it!
That purifier body of yours, O Agni, which entered into the atmosphere, which is in the wind, which is in the vāmadevya, which is in the triṣṭubh meter, which is in the fifteenfold stoma, that of yours I win through this.
Svāhā to it!
That bright body of yours, O Agni, which entered into heaven, which is in the sun, which is in the bṛhat, which is in the jagatī meter, which is in the seventeenfold stoma, that of yours I win through this.
Svāhā to it!

तद् अयम् आत्मा /
पुरीषम् असि संप्रियः पशुभिः /
यच्छा तोकाय तनयाय शं योः /
घर्मः शिरः /
तद् अयम् अग्निः /
पुरीषम् असि संप्रियः पशुभिः /
स्वदितं नः पितुं पच /
अर्कश् चक्षुः /
तद् असौ सूर्यः /
पुरीषम् असि संप्रियः पशुभिः /
यत् ते शुक्र शुक्रं धाम शुक्रा तनूः शुक्रं ज्योतिर् अजस्रं यत् ते ऽनाधृष्टम् नामानाधृष्यं तेन त्वादधे //
द्यौर् मह्नासि भूमिर् भूम्ना /
तस्यास् ते देव्य् अदित उपस्थे ऽन्नादम् अन्नाद्यायान्नपत्यायादधे //
आयं गौः पृश्निर् अक्रमीद् असदन् मातरं पुरः /
पितरं च प्रयन्त् स्वः //
अस्य प्राणाद् अपानत्य् अन्तश् चरति रोचना /
व्यख्यन् महिषो दिवम् //
त्रिंशद् धाम विराजति वाक् पतङ्गा अशिश्रयुः /
प्रति वस्तोर् अह द्युभिः //
text_mt:
Wind is breath.
Then this is the self.
You are Purīṣya, well-loved by cattle.
Extend peace and prosperity to children and offspring.
The gharma is the head.
Then this is Agni.
You are Purīṣya, well-loved by cattle.
Cook our food seasoned with sweetness.
The sun is the eye.
Then that is the sun.
You are Purīṣya, well-loved by cattle.
Whatever bright abode is yours, O bright one, whatever bright body, whatever bright, unceasing light, whatever unassailable, invincible name is yours, therewith I establish you.
You are heaven in greatness, the earth in expanse.
On the lap of you, divine Aditi, I establish [you], the eater of food, for food, for the lordship of food.
This spotted bull has stepped forth, he has sat down before the mother,
and going forth to the father, heaven.
By his out-breathing she breathes in; the radiant one moves within;
the buffalo looked forth to heaven.
Speech shines across thirty domains; the birds have settled [upon them],
day by day through the skies, towards the dawn.

meaning:
अदितिर् वै प्रजाकामौदनम् अपचत् /
तस्योच्छिष्टम् आश्नात् /
सा गर्भम् अधत्त /
तत आदित्या अजायन्त /

आक्रमणम् एव /

ताभ्याम् एवैनं तनूभ्यां संगमयति /
निर्मार्गस्यादधाति /
अपगूर्त्या वै वीर्यं क्रियते /
यन् निर्मार्गस्यादधाति /
अपगूर्त्या एव /
संवत्सरो वै प्रजननम् अग्निः प्रजनयिता /
तत् प्रजननम् /
यत् पुरा संवत्सराद् अग्नौ समिध आदधाति /
प्रजननाद् एवैनं प्रजनयिता प्रजनयति /
अभक्तर्तुर् वै पुरुषः /
न हि तद् वेद यम् ऋतुम् अभिजायते यन् नक्षत्रम् /
यत् समिध आदधाति
य एवास्यर्तुर् यन् नक्षत्रं तद् आप्नोति /
य एष ओदनः पच्यते
योनिर् एवैष क्रियते /
यत् समिध आधीयन्ते

ता हि संवत्सरस्य प्रतिमा /
अथो तिसृष्व् अथो द्वयोर् अथो पूर्वेद्युर्
आधेयास् त्व् एवाग्निम् आदधानेन /
आदित्या वा इत उत्तमा अमुं लोकम् आयन् /
ते पथिरक्षयः /
त इयक्षमाणं प्रतिनुदन्ते /
उच्छेषणभागा वा आदित्याः /
यद् उच्छिष्टेन समिधो ऽनक्ति
तेभ्य एव प्रावोचत /
तेभ्य एव प्रोच्य स्वर्गं लोकम् आरोहति //
text_mt:
Aditi, desirous of offspring, cooked porridge.
She ate its remnant.
She conceived a womb.
From it the Ādityas were born.
This porridge that is cooked is just an undertaking,
just a stepping onto.
The kindling-sticks are a span in length.
For of such a measure is the self, commensurate with Prajāpati.
Agni united with that sacrificial body of his which was in the aśvattha tree.
This is his buttery body, namely butter.
When he anoints the kindling-sticks with butter,
he unites him with just those two bodies of his.
He puts them on vigorously.
For valor is displayed by rearing up.
When he puts them on vigorously,
[it is] indeed by rearing up.
The year is reproduction; Agni is the procreator.
That is reproduction.
When he places the kindling-sticks on the fire before a year [has passed],
the procreator generates him from reproduction itself.
Man is indeed devoid of an allocated season.
For he does not know under which season he is born, under which asterism.
When he places the kindling-sticks,
he reaches whatever is his season, whatever is his asterism.
This porridge that is cooked,
this is made into a womb.
When the kindling-sticks are laid down,
it is seed that is thereby deposited.
In a year, seed that has been deposited produces offspring.
When he establishes the fire when the year has come to an end,
he establishes him when he is born.
They are to be placed twelve nights before.
For they are the image of the year.
Or on three [nights], or on two, or on the previous day;
but they must certainly be placed by one who is establishing the fire.
The Ādityas went from here to that highest world.
They are the path-guards.
They push back one who desires to sacrifice.
The Ādityas have the remnants as their share.
When he anoints the kindling-sticks with the remnant,
he has announced it to them.
Having announced it to them, he ascends to the heavenly world.

text_mt:
The directions indeed were not arranged, nor were they discerned.
Then they made this eastern direction shine for Agni, which is the Kṛttikās.
When he establishes the fire under the Kṛttikās,
he establishes it in the eastern direction.
He alone settles facing east who has established his sacred fires;
the others face west.
This asterism, namely the Kṛttikās, belongs to Agni.
When he establishes the fire under the Kṛttikās,
he establishes it in its own asterism.
The head of Prajāpati is indeed the Kṛttikās.
When he establishes the fire under the Kṛttikās,
he becomes head, foremost.
The Kṛttikās are seven.
Seven are the vital breaths in the head.
The vital breaths are the faculties of sense.
He obtains the vital breaths, the faculties of sense.
[He should establish it under Rohiṇī.]
Under Rohiṇī the gods established it.
Through it they made [the sacrifice] ascend the ascent.
That is the Rohiṇī-nature of Rohiṇī.
Under Rohiṇī Prajāpati established it.
Through it he made [it] ascend the ascent.
That is the Rohiṇī-nature of Rohiṇī.
This indeed is man's heavenly world, that he becomes more prosperous in this world.
For prosperity alone should he establish it under Rohiṇī.
The Asuras were named Kālakāñjas.
They piled up bricks.
Then Indra laid an extra brick there.
A pair of them mounted to heaven.
Then he pulled it out.
They were scattered downward.
Those two are the heavenly dogs.
He who was torn apart is that spider which strives to stretch [a web] with his own entrails.
He took away their force and vigor.
He takes away the force and vigor of his rival when he establishes the fire under Citrā.
That is this asterism belonging to Indra, full of overcoming power.
He who desires, “May I be fortunate,” should establish it under the Pūrvā Phalgunīs.
This asterism belongs to Bhaga.
He becomes fortunate.
He who desires, “May my offspring be eager to give,” should establish it under the Uttarā [Phalgunīs].
This asterism belongs to Aryaman.
He who gives is Aryaman.
These offspring subsist on gifts.
They become eager to give to him.
He should establish it for a nobleman.
For a nobleman subsists on giving.
It should be established by a Brahmin in spring.
Spring is indeed the Brahmin's season.
He establishes it in his own season.
He takes up fiery energy and spiritual luster.
It should be established by a nobleman in summer.
Summer is indeed the nobleman's season.
He establishes it in his own season.
He takes up force and vigor.
It should be established by a commoner in autumn.
Autumn is indeed the commoner's season.
He establishes it in his own season.
He takes up nourishment and cattle.
He establishes the fire thinking, “May I sacrifice with Soma.”
One about to sacrifice with Soma should establish it in any season whatsoever.
For he who sacrifices with Soma has made it grow.
It should be established at the full moon of Phalgunī.
This is the mouth of the seasons.
He establishes it at the mouth of the seasons.
[It should be established in the cold season.]
[The cold season is the birthplace of Agni.]
[He establishes him as soon as born.]
He establishes the fire thinking, “May I prosper in all directions.”
In the cold season Agni is in all directions.
He prospers in all directions who establishes the fire in the cold season.
He should establish it at the full moon or at the new moon.
This is an auspicious day.
He establishes it on an auspicious day.
Therefore he should sacrifice with an iṣṭi, or with the first-fruits offering, or with an animal, or with Soma, at the full moon or at the new moon.
This indeed is sacrifice.
He undertakes sacrifice face to face with sacrifice.

When these two [worlds] drifted apart, whatever sacrificial essence belonged to that one was emitted toward this one: the saline earth.
Since there is saline earth,
he establishes him in the sacrificial essence of these two.
These indeed belong to Prajāpati.
Day by day they become more numerous.
They serve for procreation.
This indeed is the favorite abode of cattle.
Since there is saline earth,
he attains the favorite abode of cattle.
This earth indeed trembled.
She feared: "Agni will burn me excessively."
He feared: "Agni will remove my heat."
For she was moist, as it were.
The gods made her firm with pebbles.
They placed brilliance into Agni.
Since there are pebbles,
he makes this [earth] firm;
he places brilliance into Agni.
She was touched by Vṛtra.
Only the ants know where her living, sacrificial essence is.
Since there is an ant-hill earth-mound,
he establishes him in the living, sacrificial essence of this [earth].
Waters indeed were this [universe],
only a flood. Prajāpati, having become a boar, dived down.
As much earth as his mouth could hold, so much he brought up.
That became this [earth].
Since there is earth thrown up by a boar,
he establishes him directly in this [earth].
A boar indeed sees food in her;
for him she yields.
Since there is earth thrown up by a boar,
he secures that very food.
Because he took it (ādatta), it became Aditi; because it spread (aprathata), it became the earth (pṛthivī); because it came into being (abhavat), it became the ground (bhūmi).
Since there is earth thrown up by a boar,
he expands with offspring and cattle.
Different indeed are the foods of animals: one is the food of the cow, another of the horse, another of the sheep, another of the goat, another of man.
Water is food.
When he pours water on,
he secures all food.
These are the five materials.
Five indeed are the vital powers in man.
He performs valor with this one, he performs valor with this one, he performs valor with this one.
He attains all vital power.
These are the five materials.
Fivefold is the sacrifice.
He secures the sacrifice.
Food does not satisfy without vigor.
Vigor is the udumbara tree.
Since [the woods] are from the udumbara tree,
he places vigor in food.
They are made of śamī wood
for pairing.
When Agni was created, Prajāpati kindled him at first with the śamī.
Since they are made of śamī wood,
he kindles him with his own kindling-stick.
Agni, having become a horse, ran away from the gods.
Where he stood, there the aśvattha tree arose.
That is the aśvattha nature of the aśvattha tree.
Since [the woods] are from the aśvattha tree,
whatever of him was left there, that he gathers with them.
Agni ran away from the gods with human beings.
The gods thought: "He will become this [world]."
The Maruts tore out his heart with thunder.
That became the divine lightning.
Since they are from a tree struck by lightning,
whatever of him was left there, that he gathers with them.
Those of parṇa wood are the fifth
for fivefoldness.

At eight paces [the fire] should be established by a brāhmaṇa.
The gāyatrī has eight syllables.
The brāhmaṇa has the gāyatrī metre.
He establishes him along the course of his own metre.
As a father invigorates his son, so his own metre invigorates him.
At eleven paces [the fire] should be established by a rājanya.
The triṣṭubh has eleven syllables.
The rājanya has the triṣṭubh metre.
He establishes him along the course of his own metre.
As a father invigorates his son, so his own metre invigorates him.
[At twelve paces it should be established by a vaiśya.]
[The jagatī has twelve syllables.]
[The vaiśya has the jagatī metre.]
[He establishes him along the course of his own metre.]
[As a father invigorates his son, so his own metre invigorates him.]
"May I secure the unmeasured," thus indeed he establishes the fire.
It should be established at an unmeasured [distance]
for the securing of the unmeasured.
At whatever distance he may perceive with his eye, at so great [a distance] he should establish it.
Truth indeed is the eye.
In truth he establishes it.
In the morning it should be established.
This indeed is an auspicious day.
On an auspicious day he establishes it.
At dawn, before the rising of the sun, it should be established.
In this realm Prajāpati created offspring.
They were born.
Only for procreation should it be established.
The night belongs to Agni, the day to Indra.
If he were to establish it when the sun has risen, he would depart from the colour of Agni;
if when it has not risen, from that of Indra.
The western [fire] should be established when [the sun] has not risen, the eastern when it has risen.
He attains both the colours of Indra and Agni.
The night is asuric by colour, the day bright.
He establishes it in brightness when he establishes it when the sun has risen.
By night [it is established] when [the sun] has not risen, by day when it has risen.
He establishes it by day when he establishes it when the sun has risen.
Human beings do not clearly know the asterism, as it were;
for they deliberate, as it were; but through [the sun] risen there is an auspicious day.
On an auspicious day he establishes it when he establishes it when the sun has risen.
"Seven are your kindling-sticks, O Agni, seven your tongues, seven the seers, seven the dear abodes;
knowing the seven hotrās, fill the seven wombs with butter."
Thus [he says].
As many as are the bodies of Agni,
whoever, establishing him, makes them thirsty, indeed becomes thirsty.
So many are the bodies of Agni: seven by seven in sixfold division.
He gratifies these of his;
he does not become thirsty.
He offers with a full ladle.
Prajāpati is full.
He attains Prajāpati.

इडा वै मनाव् आसीत् /

अग्निर् ब्रह्म /

text_mt: "I establish thee with the vow of the divine Aṅgirases," [saying this, the fire] is to be established by a brāhmaṇa. Those gods who are the Aṅgirases are the corresponding deities of the brāhmaṇa: Agni, Vāyu, Speech, Bṛhaspati. His sacrifice has its kinship thence, its origin thence. Exactly where his sacrifice has its kinship, whence its origin, thence he receives him. "I establish thee with the vow of Indra accompanied by the Maruts," [saying this, the fire] is to be established by a rājanya. Those gods who are kings are the corresponding deities of the rājanya: Indra, Varuṇa, Dhātṛ, Tvaṣṭṛ. His sacrifice has its kinship thence, its origin thence. Exactly where his sacrifice has its kinship, whence its origin, thence he receives him. "I establish thee with the vow of the headman Manu," [saying this, the fire] is to be established by a vaiśya. The Maruts indeed are the people among the gods. They are the corresponding deities of the vaiśya. His sacrifice has its kinship thence, its origin thence. Exactly where his sacrifice has its kinship, whence its origin, thence he receives him. Iḍā indeed was with Manu. She went to the Asuras when they were establishing the fire. They established the Āhavanīya first, then the Gārhapatya, then the porridge-cooking [fire]. She said to them: "Having reached prosperity, they climbed down; they will become auspicious, but they will perish." She went to the gods when they were establishing the fire. They established the porridge-cooking [fire] first, then the Gārhapatya, then the Āhavanīya. She said to them: "They reached prosperity, but cut off this world; they will become auspicious, but they will have no offspring." That very Iḍā established [the fires] for Manu. She said: "In such a way will I establish the fire for thee that humans will be born after the gods." She established the Gārhapatya first, then the porridge-cooking [fire], then the Āhavanīya, for the separation of these two worlds. Thence humans were born after the gods. Thus it is to be established for procreation; and also for the separation of these two worlds. When Prajāpati uttered in the beginning, he uttered truth indeed. He uttered this thrice indeed: "bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svar." This indeed is the truth of speech. With whatever is the truth of speech, with that he establishes [it]. Truth indeed brings prosperity. He who knowing thus establishes [it] with this, prospers indeed. This latter [fire] is bhūḥ; that former one is bhuvaḥ. "Bhūr bhuvaḥ"—with this the latter is to be established, so that the truth is not extinguished. "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svar"—the former [is to be established]. Thereby all that is won in front. Speech indeed disowned the deity. For speech has its deity disowned. Then all that is not truth which one curses by speech, which becomes quick. That deity which speech disowned—that is these mystical utterances indeed. This indeed is the godly part of speech. With whatever is the godly part of speech, with that he establishes [it]. This latter is bhūḥ; that former is bhuvaḥ. With "bhūr bhuvaḥ" the latter is to be established. Together indeed he establishes both of them. For this is the womb of that; from this indeed that is emitted forth. That which is the second light, that indeed is it. With "bhūr bhuvaḥ svar" the former is to be established. Together indeed he establishes both of them. For this is the womb of that; from this indeed that is brought forward. This fire indeed is that which is the fire within. That which is former, that is that sun which is brought forward from that one. That which is the third light, that indeed is reached by that. That sun indeed is established facing west. Therefore he faces all creatures westward. By means of Agni the gods eat food. Food indeed is eaten facing west. That it is established facing west is for the eating of food. Facing east Prajāpati created the gods; facing west, the Asuras. He repelled the Asuras with the sacred formulation. Agni is the sacred formulation. That it is established facing west is for repelling the rival. With the fire they go around this side; they serve this side. Around the side of the gods they go; the side of the gods they serve. Turning towards this direction he sacrifices. For the gods are in this direction. In whichever direction the gods are, turning towards that direction he sacrifices.

स्तोमाद् अश्वः संभूतः /
यद् अश्वं पुरो नयन्ति
स्तोमपुरोगा एवैभ्यो लोकेभ्यो भ्रातृव्यं प्रणुदते /
अग्निं वै जातं रक्षांस्य् अधूर्वन् /
तान्य् एनम् अभिसमलभन्त /
तान्य् अश्वेनापाहत /
यद् अश्वं पुरो नयन्ति
रक्षसाम् अपहत्यै /
अश्वो वै भूत्वा यज्ञो मनुष्यान् अत्यक्रामत् /
तम् एतम् अतिक्रामन्तं मन्यन्ते /
यद् अश्वम् अभ्यावर्तयन्ति
यज्ञम् एवैतद् यजमानम् अभ्यावर्तयन्ति /
अग्निर् वा अश्वं प्राविशत् /
कृष्णो भूत्वा सो ऽत्रागच्छद् यत्रैष मृगशफः /
तस्माद् आक्रम्यः /
यद् अश्वम् आक्रमयति
तम् एवावरुन्द्धे /
वास्तु वा एतत् /
अथो अन्तर्हितम् इव /
तस्मान् नाक्रम्यम् /
इन्द्रो वै यतीन् सालावृकेयेभ्यः प्रायच्छत् /
तेषाम् अद्यमानानां स्यूमरश्मिर् ऋषिर् अश्वं प्राविशत् /
तस्माद् अश्वः स्वं शकृद् उपजिघ्रति कच्चिद् ऋषिः चाग्निं च न निरास्थाम् इति /
अग्निं वै विभाजं नाशक्नुवन् /
तम् अश्वेन व्यभजन् /
यद् अश्वं पुरो नयन्ति /
अग्नेर् एव विभक्त्यै /
यौ वाव ताव् ऋषिश् चाग्निश् च ते एवैनं तद् देवते विभजतः /
अश्वो देयः /
प्राजापत्यो वा अश्वः /
यद् अश्वं ददाति
सर्वा एवास्य देवता अभीष्टाः प्रीता भवन्ति /
परमा वा एषा दक्षिणा यद् अश्वः /
यद् अश्वं ददाति
पर्याप्त्यै /
वही देयः /
वहिनो वै पशवो भुञ्जन्ति /
यज्ञो ऽग्नेर् वही /
भुनक्त्य् एनम् अग्निर् आहितः /
हिरण्यं देयम् /
सतेजस्त्वाय /
शतमानम् /
वीरं वा एष जनयति यो ऽग्निम् आधत्ते /
शतदायो वीरः /
त्रिंशन्माने पूर्वयोर् हविषोर् देये /
चत्वारिंशन्मानम् उत्तमे /
अभिक्रान्त्यै /
अभिक्रान्तेन हि यज्ञस्यर्ध्नोति /
आत्मा वै हविः /
पवित्रं हिरण्यम् /
सर्वेष्व् एवैनं हविःषु पुनाति /
अग्निर् वै वरुणानीर् अभ्यकामयत /
तस्य तेजः परापतत् /
तद् धिरण्यम् अभवत् /
यद् धिरण्यम् उपास्यति
स्वेनैवैनं तेजसा समर्धयति /
नोपास्य पुनर् आदधीत /
ग्रसितम् अस्य निष्खिदति क्षोधुको भवति /
अग्निं वै वरुणानीर् अभ्यकामयन्त /
आपो वरुणानीः /
ताः समभवत् /
यद् अग्ने रेतो ऽसिच्यत तद् धरितम् अभवत् /
यद् अपां तद् रजतम् /
तस्माद् धरितरजताभ्याम् उभयाहिरण्यः /
यद् गर्भस्य शमलं तद् दुर्वर्णम् /
तस्माद् ब्राह्मणेन दुर्वर्णं न भर्तव्यम् /
शमलं हि तत् /
यद् धिरण्यम् उपास्यति
स्वेनैवैनं रेतसा समर्धयति //
text_mt: Agni indeed did not desire to go forth toward the east. / They bore him forth with a horse. / That they bore [him] forth in front, that is the front-drawing nature of the front-drawer. / Agni indeed is Prajāpati. / The horse is his eye. / Since they lead a horse in front, / seeing his own eye, he goes up after [it]. / Preceded by the stoma, the gods drove out the Asuras from these worlds. / The horse was produced from the stoma. / Since they lead a horse in front, / preceded by the stoma, he drives out the rival from these worlds. / When Agni was born, the demons harmed [him]. / They took hold of him together. / He smote them away with a horse. / Since they lead a horse in front, / [it is] for the smiting away of the demons. / Having become a horse, the sacrifice crossed beyond men. / Him they consider as crossing beyond. / Since they turn the horse toward [the sacrificer], / they turn the sacrifice toward the sacrificer. / Agni indeed entered the horse. / Having become black, he came here where this deer-hoof [print] is. / Therefore it is to be trodden upon. / Since he causes the horse to tread upon it, / he secures him. / This is indeed a homestead. / Moreover, it is concealed, as it were. / Therefore it is not to be trodden upon. / Indra indeed gave over the yatis to the wild dogs. / As they were being eaten, the sage Syūmaraśmi entered the horse. / Therefore the horse sniffs its own dung, [thinking:] "Have I not thrown out the sage and Agni?" / They were indeed unable to divide Agni. / They divided him with a horse. / Since they lead a horse in front, / [it is] for the division of Agni. / Whichever two are the sage and Agni, those two deities divide him then. / A horse is to be given. / For the horse belongs to Prajāpati. / Since he gives a horse, / all his deities are desired and pleased. / The horse is the highest sacrificial gift. / Since he gives a horse, / [it is] for sufficiency. / A draught-animal is to be given. / For cattle enjoy draught-animals. / The sacrifice is Agni's draught-animal. / Agni, when established, benefits him. / Gold is to be given / for having brilliance. / [It is] of a hundred measures. / He who establishes the fire indeed engenders a hero. / A hero has a hundredfold portion. / Two [pieces] of thirty measures are to be given at the first two oblations; / one of forty measures at the last, / for advancement. / For by what advances, one prospers with the sacrifice. / The oblation is the self. / Gold is the purifier. / In all the oblations, he purifies him. / Agni indeed lusted after the wives of Varuṇa. / His brilliance flew away. / That became gold. / Since he throws gold [into the fire], / he makes him prosper with his own brilliance. / Having thrown it, he should not establish it again. / [Else] he tears away what was swallowed by him, [and] becomes hungry. / The wives of Varuṇa indeed lusted after Agni. / The waters are the wives of Varuṇa. / He copulated with them. / The seed of Agni that was poured out became yellow [gold]. / That of the waters became silver. / Therefore gold is of two kinds, yellow and silver. / The impurity of the embryo became base metal. / Therefore base metal should not be maintained by a brāhmaṇa, / for that is impurity. / Since he throws gold, / he makes him prosper with his own seed.

text_mt: Together indeed are these bodies of Agni: / this [earth] is the porridge-cooking [fire], the intermediate space is the Gārhapatya, the sky is the Āhavanīya. / Whoever establishes [the fires] without separating these [bodies] of his is not separated from evil; Rudra becomes the slayer of his cattle. / Having separated them and established them each according to its origin, he establishes [them]; he is separated from evil; Rudra does not become the slayer of his cattle. / "Thou art the sky in greatness"—[saying this,] / having established the fire, he becomes great. / "The earth in breadth"—[saying this,] / day by day he becomes greater. / "On the lap of thee, the divine Aditi, I establish [thee], the eater of food, for the eating of food, for the lordship of food." / He establishes him as the eater of food, for the eating of food, for the lordship of food. / He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire eats food. / "This spotted cow hath stepped forward"—these are the verses of the Serpent Queen. / This [earth] indeed is the Serpent Queen. / Food belongs to the Serpent Queen. / For the eating of food he establishes the fire. / He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire eats food. / The spring confines these creatures for the summer; / the summer for the rains; / the rains for the autumn; / the autumn for the winter; / the winter for the cool season; / the cool season for Agni; / Agni for the sacrificer. / He who, knowing thus, establishes the fire eats food. / A he-goat is to be given / for having the same origin. / A garment is to be given. / The garment belongs to all the gods; / [it is] for the attainment of the deities. / An increasing sacrificial gift is to be given. / The sacrificer indeed prospers according to the increase of the sacrificial gift. / A sacrificial gift that brings [further wealth] is to be given. / The milch cow is indeed that which brings [further wealth], / for she brings milk. / Nothing becomes less for him as he establishes the fire. / He should give a milch cow to the Hotṛ / for the securing of blessings; / a draft ox to the Adhvaryu: / he secures the draft-bearer of the sacrifice. / A chariot is to be given. / This sacrifice that is yoked is indeed a chariot of the gods. / With a human chariot he mounts upon the chariot of the gods. / A pair of cattle is to be given / for the securing of a pair. / Six are to be given; / six indeed are the seasons; / he is established firmly in the seasons. / Twelve are to be given; / twelve months make a year; / [it is] for the attainment of the year. / If he exceeds twelve, he should give twenty-four. / The gāyatrī has twenty-four syllables; / the gāyatrī is the mouth of the sacrifice. / He does not go beyond the gāyatrī, the mouth of the sacrifice.

सो ऽग्निर् विजयम् उपयत्सु त्रेधा तन्वो विन्यधत्त पशुषु तृतीयम् अप्सु तृतीयम् अमुष्मिन्न् आदित्ये तृतीयम् /
यद् एतानि हवींषि निरुप्यन्ते
ता एवास्यैतत् तन्वः संभरति /
[ सतनूर् एवैतत् सतेजा आधीयते / ]
[ इमे वै लोका एतानि हवींषि / ]
[ ना]नाबर्हींषि भवन्ति /
इमान् एव लोकान् आप्नोति /
यन् नानाबर्हींषि
लोकं प्रजननाय /
नोच्छिनष्टि /
ऊनं वै प्रजा उपप्रजायन्ते /
समानबर्हिषी उत्तरे कार्ये /
लोकम् एव प्रजननायाकः /
तम् उपप्रजायते /
विद्म वा अमुं लोकं विद्ममं नामुं पश्यामो वा न वा /
तस्मात् समानबर्हिषी उत्तरे कार्ये /
पशवो वा एतानि हवींषि /
घृतं पुरोडाशः /
रुद्रो ऽग्निः /
यद् अम्नो ऽनुनिर्वपेद् रुद्राय पशून् अपिदध्याद् अपशुः स्यात् /
संवत्सरे ऽनुनिरुप्याणि /
संवत्सरेणैवैनं शमयति /
शिथिलं वा एतद् यज्ञस्य क्रियते ऽसयोनि यत् संवत्सरे ऽनुनिर्वपति /
अम्न एवानुनिरुप्याणि /
अशिथिलत्वाय सयोनित्वाय //
text_mt: There are three oblations. / Three are these worlds. / He attains just these worlds. / Thrice the Virāj strode out. / Following the stride of the Virāj, he causes him to stride. / Because it is for the Purifying [Agni], it purifies him; / by that indeed [it purifies] him. / Because it is for the Cleansing [Agni], / by that he gives him food. / Because it is for the Bright [Agni], / by that he makes him fit for sacrifice, worthy of the sacrifice. / One establishes the fire thinking, "May I possess cattle, may I possess offspring, may I possess splendor." / The breath indeed is the Purifying one. / From the breath cattle are born. / Since [the oblation is] for Agni Pavamāna, / by that he generates cattle for him. / The waters indeed are the cleansing ones. / From the waters offspring are born. / Since [the oblation is] for Agni Pāvaka, / by that he generates offspring for him. / That sun yonder indeed is bright. / He is the giver of splendor. / Since [the oblation is] for Agni Śuci, / that sun yonder bestows splendor upon him. / The gods and the Asuras were in conflict. / Agni, when they were going toward victory, distributed his bodies threefold: a third among cattle, a third in the waters, a third in that sun yonder. / When these oblations are set out, / it is those bodies of his that he gathers together. / [Possessing his body, possessing his splendor, he is established.] / [These worlds indeed are these oblations.] / There are different barhis-grasses. / He attains just these worlds. / In that there are different barhis-grasses, / [he leaves] space for procreation; / he does not leave [anything] out. / Offspring are born into the deficient. / The latter two [oblations] should be made with the same barhis. / He has made space for procreation; / into that it is born. / We know yonder world, we know this one; we do not see yonder one, or we do. / Therefore the latter two [oblations] should be made with the same barhis. / Cattle indeed are these oblations; / the cake is ghee; / Agni is Rudra. / If he were to offer [them] immediately afterward, he would hand over cattle to Rudra; he would be without cattle. / They are to be offered after a year. / He appeases him by means of a year. / What is offered after a year is made slack in the sacrifice, having a different womb. / They are to be offered immediately afterward, / for the sake of unslackness, for the sake of having the same womb.

गच्छति प्रतिष्ठाम् /

text_mt: The oblation is set out, brought near, [yet] unsprinkled. / Then, having sprinkled the central gaming ground and thrown down the dice, / "Varuṇa of firm vows has sat down / in the farmsteads, wise, for sovereignty," / [saying this,] he offers into the central gaming ground. / Thrice indeed the Virāj strode out: the Gārhapatya, the Āhavanīya, the central gaming ground. / Following the stride of the Virāj, he causes him to stride. / He stands firm; / he goes to a firm footing. / He offers for the maintenance of order; / he makes him maintainer of order, Savitṛ the sustainer. / They kill a cow. / They gamble for it. / They present it to the members of the assembly. / By that, this [fire] of his becomes desired and pleased. / "Now indeed Brahmaṇaspati speaks the mantra, worthy of praise, / in which Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, the gods, have made their dwellings," / [saying this,] he offers into the addressing [fire] with [a verse] containing [the word] "mantra" and addressed to the All-Gods. / He takes up the mantra for him. / Going together to him, they take counsel. / Together indeed were the gods and men at the porridge-cooking [fire]. / Those men overstepped the gods. / The gods, pushing back food from them, strode up to the Gārhapatya. / They followed after them to that. / Those men indeed overstepped the gods. / The gods, pushing back cattle from them, strode up to the Āhavanīya. / They followed after them to that. / Those men indeed overstepped the gods. / The gods, pushing back the sacrifice from them, strode up to the assembly. / They followed after them to that. / Those men indeed overstepped the gods. / The gods, pushing back the Virāj from them, strode up to the addressing [fire]. / Thence they did not move after them. / These are the steps of the gods. / He who knows thus strides up to a better and better world. / This addressing [fire] is the unconquered truth of the gods. / Therefore one should go early in the morning to the addressing [fire]; / he goes to truth itself. / Therefore one should not go uncalled to the addressing [fire]. / Therefore one should not speak untruth at the addressing [fire]. / The carrier indeed is the porridge-cooking [fire] by name; / a carrier is born to him who knows thus. / The Gārhapatya is houses; / he becomes possessed of houses who knows thus. / The Āhavanīya is dhiṣṇya-hearths; / the sacrifice inclines toward him who knows thus. / The central gaming ground is unextendedness; / he extends with offspring and with cattle who knows thus. / The addressing [fire] is unattainable; / whoever seeks to attain him does not attain him, who knows thus.

meaning:
अग्निर् वा इमं लोकं नोपाकामयत /
यद् अस्मिन्न् आमं मांसं पचन्ति यत् पुरुषं दहन्ति यत् स्तेयं पचन्ति तद् अभीमं लोकं नोपाकामयत /

या पावकापस् तया प्राविशत् /

प्राणो वै पवमानः /
प्राणेन पशवो यताः /
यद् अग्नये पवमानाय
पशून् एवास्मै तेन यच्छति /

एषा वा अस्य सा तनूर् यापः प्राविशत् / यद् इदम् अप्सु परीव दृशे

इमे वै लोका एतानि हवींषि /
नानाबर्हींषि भवन्ति /
नाना हीमे लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः //
text_mt: Agni indeed did not desire this world. / Because they cook raw meat on it, because they burn a man, because they cook stolen goods, on account of that he did not desire this world. / When he turned toward this world, he departed with those bodies of his that were fit for sacrifice. / These are they: the Purifying, the Cleansing, the Bright. / That which was his purifying body entered the cattle with it. / That which was cleansing entered the waters with it. / That which was bright entered yonder sun with it. / The breath indeed is the Purifying one. / By breath cattle are held together. / In that [an offering is made] to Agni Pavamāna, / thereby he gives cattle to him. / This indeed is that body of his which entered the cattle, when this flame flares up, as it were, towards [the person] when ghee is offered. / This indeed is that body of his which entered the waters, when this [reflection] appears all around in the waters, as it were; / when, having washed his hands and bathed, he places faith, as it were, [in them]— / whatever fire is in the waters, that alone purifies him then, that makes [it] savory. / In that [an offering is made] to Agni Pāvaka, / along with cattle he purifies him. / This indeed is that body of his which entered the waters, when this flame flares up red, as it were, when ghee is offered. / This indeed is that body of his which entered yonder sun, which shines through from above, which became light. / In that [an offering is made] to Agni Śuci, / [it is] for manifestation, for renown, for praise, for splendor. / This indeed is that body of his which entered yonder sun, when this flame flares up golden, as it were, when ghee is offered. / In that these oblations are set out, / possessing his bodies and possessing splendor he is established. / These worlds indeed are these oblations. / They have distinct strew-grasses, / for these worlds are established distinctly.

te vīryakṛtaḥ
agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ 'nunirvapet /
āgneyo vai brāhmaṇaḥ /
devatayā somarājā /
yajñamukham agnyādheyam /
yajñamukham evākramya svārājyam upaiti /

te 'bruvan yuvāṃ vai no 'gre yajño 'bhyanān yuvayor no 'dhi yajño 'bhinamatv iti /

yad agnīṣomīyam anunirvapati
yajñasyābhinatyai /
ato hi devān agre yajño 'bhyanamat /

mithunaṃ vā agniś ca somaś ca /
somo retodhā agniḥ prajanayitā /
agnir vāvedaṃ sarvam /

etau vai no devānāṃ nediṣṭham /

te 'cikayur uddhṛtena vā anenābhijayemeti /
tam udaharanta /
tenābhyajayan /
abhijityā evaiṣa uddhriyate /
agnir vai nirādhānād abibhet /

meaning:
गायत्रीः संयाज्या भवन्ति /
गायत्रो वा अग्निर् गायत्रच्छन्दाः /
आग्नेयम् एतत् क्रियते यद् अग्न्याधेयम् /
अग्नाव् एवैतद् अग्निः प्रतितिष्ठन्न् एति यद् आग्नेयानि हवींषि /
अग्निनाग्निः समिध्यत इत्य् उत्तरयोर् हविषोर् अनुवाक्यां कुर्यात्
तेजस आयतनाय /
उर्वशी देवी पुरूरवस्यासीत् /
सान्तर्वती देवान् पुनः परैत् /
सो ऽदो देवेष्व् आयुर् अजायत /
ताम् अन्वागच्छत् /
तां पुनर् अयाचत /
ताम् अस्मै न पुनर् अददुः /
तस्मा आयुं प्रायच्छन्न् एष आयुर् इति /
अग्निं चोख्यम् /
उखायां समुप्यैतम् आधत्स्व तेन प्रजनिष्यस इति /
स वृक्षस्य शाखायाम् अग्निम् आसज्यायुना ग्रामम् अभ्यवैत् /
स पुनर् ऐमीत्य् एद् वृक्षस्याग्रे ऽग्निं ज्वलन्तम् /
सो ऽचिकेद् अयं वाव सो ऽग्निर् इति /
तस्यारणी आदायाग्निं मथित्वाधत्त /
तेन प्राजायत /
यद् आरोहस्यारणी भवतः
प्रजननाय /
अदित्यै घृते चरुं पशुकामो ऽनुनिर्वपेत् /
इयं वा अदितिः /
अस्याम् अधि पशवः प्रजायन्ते /
यज्ञमुखम् अग्न्याधेयम् /
यज्ञमुखम् एवालभ्य पशून् अवरुन्द्धे /
चातुष्प्राश्यो भवति /
आचतुरं हीमे पशवो द्वन्द्वं मिथुनाः /
ते वीर्यकृतः
अग्नीषोमीयम् एकादशकपालं ऽनुनिर्वपेत् /
आग्नेयो वै ब्राह्मणः /
देवतया सोमराजा /
यज्ञमुखम् अग्न्याधेयम् /
यज्ञमुखम् एवाक्रम्य स्वाराज्यम् उपैति /
देवान् वै यज्ञो नाभ्यनमत् /
ते ऽश्राम्यन् यज्ञो नो नाभिनमनीति /
सो ऽग्नीषोमाव् एवाग्रे यज्ञो ऽभ्यनमत् /
ते ऽविदुर् अग्नीषोमौ वै नो ऽग्रे यज्ञो ऽभ्यनांस् तयोर् यज्ञस्याभिनतिम् इच्छामहा इति /
ते ऽब्रुवन् युवां वै नो ऽग्रे यज्ञो ऽभ्यनान् युवयोर् नो ऽधि यज्ञो ऽभिनमत्व् इति /
ताव् अब्रूतां वार्यं वृणावहा आवाम् एवाग्र आज्यभागौ यजान् इति /
तस्माद् अग्नीषोमाव् एवाग्र आज्यभागौ यजन्ति /
वार्यवृतं ह्य् अनयोः /
यद् अग्नीषोमीयम् अनुनिर्वपति
यज्ञस्याभिनत्यै /
अतो हि देवान् अग्रे यज्ञो ऽभ्यनमत् /
यद् अन्यद् अनुनिर्वपेद् देवतया यज्ञम् अन्तर्दध्यात् /
मिथुनं वा अग्निश् च सोमश् च /
सोमो रेतोधा अग्निः प्रजनयिता /
अग्निर् वावेदं सर्वम् /
आप ओषधयो वनस्पतय्ः /
तद् एव सोमः /
एतौ वै नो देवानां नेदिष्ठम् /
एतौ हि पश्यामः /
यथा वा इदं मनुष्या उपासत एवम् एतं देवा उपासत /
ते ऽचिकयुर् उद्धृतेन वा अनेनाभिजयेमेति /
तम् उदहरन्त /
तेनाभ्यजयन् /
अभिजित्या एवैष उद्ध्रियते /
अग्निर् वै निराधानाद् अबिभेत् /
नातिदूर आधेयस् /
निराधानाय //
text_mt: The shared offering verses are gāyatrīs. / Agni is connected with the gāyatrī, having the gāyatrī metre. / That the establishing of the fires is performed belongs to Agni. / When the oblations belong to Agni, Agni goes establishing himself in Agni. / He should make "Agni is kindled by Agni" the invitatory verse for the two subsequent oblations, / for an abode of splendor. / The goddess Urvaśī was with Purūravas. / Pregnant, she went away again to the gods. / There, among the gods, Āyu was born. / He followed after her. / He begged for her again. / They did not give her back to him. / To him they gave Āyu, saying, "This is Āyu"; / and the fire in the pot, / [saying,] "Having placed it together in the pot, establish this; by it you will propagate." / Having hung the fire on the branch of a tree, he went down to the village with Āyu. / When he went back, [he saw] the fire burning on the top of the tree. / He perceived: "This indeed is that fire." / Taking its kindling sticks, having churned the fire, he established it. / By it he propagated. / In that the kindling sticks are of the āroha [tree], / it is for propagation. / One desiring cattle should offer after [the main rites] a porridge in ghee for Aditi. / This [earth] indeed is Aditi. / Upon her cattle are born. / The establishing of the fires is the mouth of the sacrifice. / Having seized the mouth of the sacrifice, he secures cattle. / It is to be eaten by four [priests], / for these cattle are fourfold, a pair, mated; / they produce virility. / He should offer after [the main rites] an eleven-pot-sherd cake to Agni and Soma. / The Brahmin belongs to Agni; / by deity he has Soma as king. / The establishing of the fires is the mouth of the sacrifice. / Having stepped onto the mouth of the sacrifice, he attains sovereignty. / The sacrifice indeed did not incline toward the gods. / They toiled, [saying,] "May the sacrifice incline toward us." / First, that sacrifice inclined toward Agni and Soma. / They knew: "The sacrifice first inclined toward Agni and Soma; let us seek the inclination of the sacrifice from the two of them." / They said: "The sacrifice first inclined toward you two; let the sacrifice incline toward us through you two." / The two said: "Let us choose a boon: may they sacrifice to us two first as the two ghee-portions." / Therefore they sacrifice first to Agni and Soma as the two ghee-portions, / for they have chosen a boon. / In that he offers after [the main rites] the cake to Agni and Soma, / it is for the inclination of the sacrifice, / for from there the sacrifice first inclined toward the gods. / If he were to offer another [oblation] after, he would separate the sacrifice from the deity. / Agni and Soma are indeed a couple; / Soma is the placer of seed, Agni the propagator. / Agni indeed is all this; / waters, plants, and trees— / that indeed is Soma. / These two of the gods are nearest to us, / for these two we see. / As men attend upon this [fire], so the gods attended upon this one. / They perceived: "With this one carried forth, let us conquer." / They carried it forth; / with it they conquered. / For conquest indeed this [fire] is carried forth. / Agni indeed feared being taken away from his establishment. / It is not to be established too far off, / [so that he is not] taken away from his establishment.

आधेयो ऽग्नी3र् नाधेया3 इति मीमांसन्ते / श्वो ऽग्निम् आधास्यमानेनेति /
आधेय एव
अयज्ञो ह्य् एष यो ऽनग्निः /
अजो बद्धस् तां रात्रीं वसेत् /
अग्नितेजसं वा अजः /
तद् एव तम् अग्निम् आधत्ते /
कल्माषः स्यात् /

यस् तं श्वो ऽग्निम् आधास्यन् स्यात् स तां रात्रीं व्रतं चरेत् /
न मांसम् अश्नीयात् /
न स्त्रीम् उपेयात् /

अग्निर् अस्माद् अपक्रामेत् /
एष ह्य् एतस्य योनिः /

agniṃ vai sṛṣṭam agnihotram anvasṛjyata /

ayathāpūrvaṃ kuryāt /
pūrṇayā srucā manasā prajāpataye juhoti /
pūrṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ /
prajāpatim evāpnoti /

pūrṇaḥ puruṣaḥ kāmair ūnaḥ samṛddhibhiḥ /

meaning:
अग्निं वै सृष्टम् अग्निहोत्रम् अन्वसृज्यत /
तस्माद् अग्निम् आहितम् अग्निहोत्रेणानूद्द्रवन्ति /
आग्नेयी सायम् आहुतिः सौरी प्रतः /
यद् आग्नेय्या प्रातर् जुहुयात् प्रजननं पुरस्तात् परिहरेत् /
अयथापूर्वं कुर्यात् /
पूर्णया स्रुचा मनसा प्रजापतये जुहोति /
पूर्णः प्रजापतिः /
प्रजापतिम् एवाप्नोति /
पूर्णो वै प्रजापतिः समृद्धिभिर् ऊनो व्यृद्धिभिः /
पूर्णः पुरुषः कामैर् ऊनः समृद्धिभिः /
पूर्णेनैव पूर्णः समृद्धीर् अवरुन्द्धे /
आनीता वा अन्येषां देवानां स्मो ऽनानीता अन्येषाम् /
संस्पर्शेनान्येषां जीवामः सकाशेनान्येषाम् /
पृथिव्या वातस्यापां तेषाम् आनीताः स्मस् तेषां संस्पर्शेन जीवामः /
अग्नेः सूर्यस्य दिवस् तेषाम् अनानीताः स्मस् तेषां सकाशेन जीवामः /
तान् एवैतद् आलब्ध /
त एनम् आनेषत /
श्रेयसो व्रातस्य भवति /
नास्य मनुष्याः पापवसीयसस्येशते /
यद् आत्मनालभेत प्रमायुकः स्यात् /
आज्येन चौषधीभिश् चालभते /
अप्रमायुको भवति /
आनीतो वा एष देवानां य आहिताग्निः /
अदन्त्य् अस्यान्नम् /
पूर्णया स्रुचा जुहोति /
पूर्णयाग्नये ऽलम् अकः /
अलम् अस्मै भवति /
ओषधयश् च वै वनस्पतयश् च दिवा समदधुः /
त इतो ऽन्यत् सर्वम् अबाधन्त /
स प्रजापतिर् अमन्यतेमे वावेदम् अभूवन्न् इति /
सो ऽग्निं सृष्ट्वा तम् आधत्त /
तेनैनान् न्यभावयत् /
भ्रातृव्यसहनो वावैष आधीयते हुताद्याय /
एष वा अहुताद्यो ऽलम् अग्न्याधेयाय सन्न् अनाहिताग्निः /
हुतम् एवैतेन स्वदितम् अत्ति //
text_mt:
When Agni was created, the Agnihotra was created after [him].
Therefore, to Agni when established, they run after with the Agnihotra.
The evening offering belongs to Agni, the morning offering to Sūrya.
If he were to offer with an [oblation] to Agni in the morning, he would turn procreation away from the front;
he would act contrary to the proper order.
With a full ladle, with the mind, he offers to Prajāpati.
Full is Prajāpati;
he attains Prajāpati.
Prajāpati is full of prosperities, empty of failures.
Man is full of desires, empty of prosperities.
By the full itself, being full, he secures prosperities.
We are brought near to some gods, not brought near to others.
Through contact we live with some, in the presence of others.
We are brought near to those of the earth, of the wind, of the waters; through contact with them we live.
We are not brought near to those of Agni, of Sūrya, of heaven; in their presence we live.
He has touched just them here;
they bring him near.
He belongs to a better company;
human beings do not have power over his relative status.
If he were to touch [them] with himself, he would be likely to die.
He touches [them] with ghee and with herbs;
he does not become likely to die.
He who has established the fires has indeed been brought near to the gods;
they eat his food.
He offers with a full ladle;
with the full ladle, he has made sufficient for Agni;
it becomes sufficient for him.
The herbs and the trees allied themselves with heaven.
They drove off everything else from here.
That Prajāpati thought: "These indeed have become this [world]."
Having created Agni, he established him;
by him he overpowered them.
He is established as one who overcomes rivals, for eating what is offered.
He who, being capable of the establishing of the fires, has not established the fires, does not eat what is offered.
By this, he eats only what is offered and seasoned.

sanskrit_iast:
ahutādo vā etasya purā devāḥ /
athaitad dhutāda upāvartate /
te 'syorjāpakrāmanti /
ūrjam evāvarunddhe /
tān eva bhāginaḥ karoti /
yajanty amuṣmiñ juhvaty asmin pacanty amuṣminn anantarayāyaitasya /
atho vaiśvānaratāyām evainam upātiṣṭhipat /
ye vai yajñenāyajantārdhnuvaṃs te /
na vai su vidur iva manuṣyā yajñam /
tasmān na sarva ivardhnoti /
yad dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti
yajñasyārdhaḥ /
dakṣiṇāvadbhyāṃ ha sma vai purā darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajante /
ya eṣa odanaḥ pacyate
dakṣiṇām evaitāṃ dadāti
yajñasyarddhyai /
iṣṭī vā etena yad yajate /
ya eṣa odanaḥ pacyate
tena pūrtī /
eṣa vāveṣṭāpūrtī ya etaṃ pacati /
prajāpatir vai devebhyo bhāgadheyāni vyādiśat /
yajñam eva so 'manyatātmānam antaragām iti /
sa etam odanam apaśyat /
tam ātmane bhāgam akalpayat /
prajāpater vāvaiṣa bhāgaḥ /
mahāntam aparimitaṃ pacet /
aparimitaḥ prajāpatiḥ /
prajāpatim evāpnoti /
devāś ca vā asurāś cāspardhanta /
te devāḥ prajāpatim evābhyayajanta /
anyo 'nyasyāsann asurā ajuhavuḥ /
te devā etam odanam apaśyan /
taṃ prajāpataye bhāgam anuniravapan /
taṃ bhāgaṃ paśyan prajāpatir devān upāvartata /
tato devā abhavan parāsurā abhavan /
ya evaṃ vidvān anvāhāryam āharati bhavaty ātmanā parāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati /
īḍyā vā anye devāḥ saparyeṇyā anye /
devā īḍyā brāhmaṇāḥ saparyeṇyāḥ /
yajñenaiveḍyān prīṇāty anvāhāryeṇa saparyeṇyān /
tasyobhaye prītā yajñe bhavanti /
prajāpater bhāgo 'sy ūrjasvān /
akṣito 'sy akṣityai tvā /
akṣito nāmāsi mā me kṣeṣṭhāḥ /
prāṇāpānau me pāhi /
udānarūpe me pāhi /
ūrg asy ūrjaṃ mayi dhehi /
prajāpatiṃ tvayā samakṣam ṛdhyāsam iti
tam eva samakṣam ṛdhnoti /
meaning:
अहुतादो वा एतस्य पुरा देवाः /
अथैतद् धुताद उपावर्तते /
ते ऽस्योर्जापक्रामन्ति /
ऊर्जम् एवावरुन्द्धे /
तान् एव भागिनः करोति /
यजन्त्य् अमुष्मिञ् जुह्वत्य् अस्मिन् पचन्त्य् अमुष्मिन्न् अनन्तरयायैतस्य /
अथो वैश्वानरतायाम् एवैनम् उपातिष्ठिपत् /
ये वै यज्ञेनायजन्तार्ध्नुवंस् ते /
न वै सु विदुर् इव मनुष्या यज्ञम् /
तस्मान् न सर्व इवर्ध्नोति /
यद् दक्षिणां ददाति
यज्ञस्यार्धः /
दक्षिणावद्भ्यां ह स्म वै पुरा दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यां यजन्ते /
य एष ओदनः पच्यते
दक्षिणाम् एवैतां ददाति
यज्ञस्यर्द्ध्यै /
इष्टी वा एतेन यद् यजते /
य एष ओदनः पच्यते
तेन पूर्ती /
एष वावेष्टापूर्ती य एतं पचति /
प्रजापतिर् वै देवेभ्यो भागधेयानि व्यादिशत् /
यज्ञम् एव सो ऽमन्यतात्मानम् अन्तरगाम् इति /
स एतम् ओदनम् अपश्यत् /
तम् आत्मने भागम् अकल्पयत् /
प्रजापतेर् वावैष भागः /
महान्तम् अपरिमितं पचेत् /
अपरिमितः प्रजापतिः /
प्रजापतिम् एवाप्नोति /
देवाश् च वा असुराश् चास्पर्धन्त /
ते देवाः प्रजापतिम् एवाभ्ययजन्त /
अन्यो ऽन्यस्यासन्न् असुरा अजुहवुः /
ते देवा एतम् ओदनम् अपश्यन् /
तं प्रजापतये भागम् अनुनिरवपन् /
तं भागं पश्यन् प्रजापतिर् देवान् उपावर्तत /
ततो देवा अभवन् परासुरा अभवन् /
य एवं विद्वान् अन्वाहार्यम् आहरति भवत्य् आत्मना परास्य भ्रातृव्यो भवति /
ईड्या वा अन्ये देवाः सपर्येण्या अन्ये /
देवा ईड्या ब्राह्मणाः सपर्येण्याः /
यज्ञेनैवेड्यान् प्रीणात्य् अन्वाहार्येण सपर्येण्यान् /
तस्योभये प्रीता यज्ञे भवन्ति /
प्रजापतेर् भागो ऽस्य् ऊर्जस्वान् /
अक्षितो ऽस्य् अक्षित्यै त्वा /
अक्षितो नामासि मा मे क्षेष्ठाः /
प्राणापानौ मे पाहि /
उदानरूपे मे पाहि /
ऊर्ग् अस्य् ऊर्जं मयि धेहि /
प्रजापतिं त्वया समक्षम् ऋध्यासम् इति
तम् एव समक्षम् ऋध्नोति /
text_mt:
Formerly, his gods did not eat what is offered.
Then he turns to those who eat what is offered.
They depart from his nourishment.
He secures nourishment;
he makes them partakers [of the share].
They sacrifice in yonder [fire], they offer into this [one], they cook in that [one], for his non-interruption.
And moreover, he made him stand firm in the state of being Vaiśvānara.
Those who sacrificed with sacrifice prospered.
Men do not quite know sacrifice well;
therefore not everyone, as it were, prospers.
When he gives a sacrificial fee,
that is half of the sacrifice.
Formerly indeed, they sacrificed with the new- and full-moon offerings accompanied by sacrificial fees.
This rice-mash which is cooked—
he gives this as the sacrificial fee
for the prosperity of the sacrifice.
One who sacrifices is an iṣṭin thereby;
this rice-mash which is cooked—
by that he is a pūrtin.
He who cooks this is an iṣṭāpūrtin.
Prajāpati indeed apportioned the shares to the gods.
He thought: "I have excluded myself from the sacrifice."
He saw this rice-mash;
he fashioned that as a share for himself.
This is indeed Prajāpati's share.
He should cook a great, immeasurable [amount];
immeasurable is Prajāpati;
he attains Prajāpati.
The gods and the Asuras contended.
Those gods sacrificed to Prajāpati;
the Asuras offered into one another's mouths.
Those gods saw this rice-mash;
they poured it out as a share for Prajāpati.
Seeing that share, Prajāpati turned to the gods.
Then the gods flourished, the Asuras were defeated.
He who, knowing thus, brings the anvāhārya becomes himself [flourishing], his rival is defeated.
Some gods are to be praised, others are to be served.
The gods are to be praised; the brahmins are to be served.
By the sacrifice he pleases those to be praised, by the anvāhārya those to be served.
Both of his become pleased at the sacrifice.
"You are Prajāpati's share, rich in vigor."
"You are undecaying; for undecayingness [I take] you."
"You are undecaying by name; do not decay for me."
"Protect my in-breath and out-breath."
"Protect the form of my upward breath."
"You are vigor; place vigor in me."
"May I prosper directly through you, [attaining] Prajāpati"—
with this, he prospers directly through him.

yat te manyuparoptasya pṛthivīm anudadhvase /
ādityā viśve tad devā vasavaḥ punar ābharan //
yat tvā kruddhaḥ parovapa manyunā yad avartyā /
sukalpam agne tat tava punas tvoddīpayāmasi //
punas tvādityā rudrā vasavaḥ samindhatāṃ punar brahmāṇo vasudhītim agne /
ihaiva dhehy adhi dakṣam ugram aśvāvad gomad yavamat suvīryam //
punas tvā mitrāvaruṇau punar indraḥ punar bhagaḥ /
punas tvā viśve devā brāhmaṇā udadīdipan //
punar ūrjā nivartasva punar agna iṣāyuṣā /
punar naḥ pāhy aṃhasaḥ //
saha rayyā nivartasvāgne pinvasva dhārayā /
viśvapsnyā viśvatas pari //
ketaḥ saketaḥ suketas te na ādityā juṣāṇā asya haviṣo vyantu svāhā /
salilaḥ saligaḥ sagaras te na ādityā juṣāṇā asya haviṣo vyantu svāhā /
divo jyotir vivasva āditya te no devā deveṣu satyāṃ devahūtim āsuvadhvam /
ādityebhyaḥ svāhā //
meaning:
यत् ते मन्युपरोप्तस्य पृथिवीम् अनुदध्वसे /
आदित्या विश्वे तद् देवा वसवः पुनर् आभरन् //
यत् त्वा क्रुद्धः परोवप मन्युना यद् अवर्त्या /
सुकल्पम् अग्ने तत् तव पुनस् त्वोद्दीपयामसि //
पुनस् त्वादित्या रुद्रा वसवः समिन्धतां पुनर् ब्रह्माणो वसुधीतिम् अग्ने /
इहैव धेह्य् अधि दक्षम् उग्रम् अश्वावद् गोमद् यवमत् सुवीर्यम् //
पुनस् त्वा मित्रावरुणौ पुनर् इन्द्रः पुनर् भगः /
पुनस् त्वा विश्वे देवा ब्राह्मणा उददीदिपन् //
पुनर् ऊर्जा निवर्तस्व पुनर् अग्न इषायुषा /
पुनर् नः पाह्य् अंहसः //
सह रय्या निवर्तस्वाग्ने पिन्वस्व धारया /
विश्वप्स्न्या विश्वतस् परि //
केतः सकेतः सुकेतस् ते न आदित्या जुषाणा अस्य हविषो व्यन्तु स्वाहा /
सलिलः सलिगः सगरस् ते न आदित्या जुषाणा अस्य हविषो व्यन्तु स्वाहा /
दिवो ज्योतिर् विवस्व आदित्य ते नो देवा देवेषु सत्यां देवहूतिम् आसुवध्वम् /
आदित्येभ्यः स्वाहा //
text_mt:
What scattered along the earth when you were cast away in anger,
that the Ādityas, the All-Gods, and the Vasus brought back again.
What, when angered, [the sacrificer] cast away from you in wrath or in distress,
let that be easily adjusted for you, O Agni; we rekindle you again.
May the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus rekindle you again, and the Brahmans again, O Agni, store of wealth;
place right here fierce, mighty ability, possessing horses, cattle, and barley, with good heroes!
Again may Mitra and Varuṇa, again Indra, again Bhaga,
again may the All-Gods and the brāhmaṇas kindle you!
Return again with nourishment, return again, O Agni, with refreshment and long life;
protect us again from distress!
Return with wealth, O Agni; swell with a stream
all-nourishing from every side!
Intention, Agreement, Right Intention, may those Ādityas enjoying this oblation partake of it, svāhā!
Salila, Saliga, Sagara, may those Ādityas enjoying this oblation partake of it, svāhā!
O Light of Heaven, shine forth, O Āditya; O you gods among the gods, impel our true invocation of the gods;
to the Ādityas, svāhā!

agner vai bhāgaḥ punarādheyam /
taṃ bhāgaṃ prepsan vyardhayati /
yady ādhāya manyeta vyṛdhyate sya iti punar ādadhīta /
yaṃ bhāgaṃ prepsan vyardhayati taṃ prāpyārdhayaty eva /
sarvam āgneyaṃ kriyate /
yad eva kiṃ ca sarvam agnaye bhāgaṃ prādāt sarvām ṛddhim ṛdhnoti /
na saṃbhārāḥ saṃbhṛtyā ity āhur na yajuḥ kāryam iti /
saṃbhṛtasaṃbhāro hy eṣa kṛtayajuḥ /
tat tan na sūrkṣyam /
saṃbhṛtyā eva saṃbhārāḥ kāryaṃ yajuḥ /
punarutsyūtaṃ vāso deyaṃ punarutsṛṣṭo 'naḍvān punarniṣkṛto rathaḥ /
etāni vai punarādheyasya rūpāṇi /
rūpair evainat samardhayati /
agnir vā utsīdann apa oṣadhīr anūtsīdati /
etā vā āpa oṣadhayo yad darbhāḥ /
yad darbhā upolapā bhavanti /
adbhya evainam oṣadhībhyo 'dhyavarunddhe //
devāś ca vā asurāś cāspardhanta /
te devā vijayam upayanto 'gnau priyās tanvaḥ saṃnyadadhata /
yadi jayememā upāvartemahi yadi no jayeyur imā abhyupadhāvemeti /
te 'bhijityānvaicchan sarveṣāṃ naḥ saheti /
so 'gnir abravīd yo mā maddevatyam ādadhātai sa etābhis tanūbhiḥ saṃbhavād iti /
taṃ devā ādadhata /
ta etābhis tanūbhiḥ samabhavan /
etābhir eva tanūbhiḥ saṃbhavati ya evaṃ vidvān etam ādhatte /
tvaṣṭā paśukāma ādhatta /
ta ime tvāṣṭrāḥ paśavaḥ /
tenarddhāḥ /
manuḥ puṣṭikāma ādhatta /
sa imān poṣān apuṣyat /
tenarddhāḥ /
prajāpatiḥ prajākāma ādhatta /
tā imāḥ prājāpatyāḥ prajāḥ prājāyanta /
tenarddhāḥ /
yo vai tam ādhatta sa tena vasunā samabhavat /
tasmāt punarvasuḥ /
tasmāt punarvasāv ādheyaḥ /
ārdhnod vai sa yas tam ādhatta /
tasmād anūrādhāḥ /
tasmād anūrādhāsv ādheyaḥ //
meaning:
अग्नेर् वै भागः पुनराधेयम् /
तं भागं प्रेप्सन् व्यर्धयति /
यद्य् आधाय मन्येत व्यृध्यते स्य इति पुनर् आदधीत /
यं भागं प्रेप्सन् व्यर्धयति तं प्राप्यार्धयत्य् एव /
सर्वम् आग्नेयं क्रियते /
यद् एव किं च सर्वम् अग्नये भागं प्रादात् सर्वाम् ऋद्धिम् ऋध्नोति /
न संभाराः संभृत्या इत्य् आहुर् न यजुः कार्यम् इति /
संभृतसंभारो ह्य् एष कृतयजुः /
तत् तन् न सूर्क्ष्यम् /
संभृत्या एव संभाराः कार्यं यजुः /
पुनरुत्स्यूतं वासो देयं पुनरुत्सृष्टो ऽनड्वान् पुनर्निष्कृतो रथः /
एतानि वै पुनराधेयस्य रूपाणि /
रूपैर् एवैनत् समर्धयति /
अग्निर् वा उत्सीदन्न् अप ओषधीर् अनूत्सीदति /
एता वा आप ओषधयो यद् दर्भाः /
यद् दर्भा उपोलपा भवन्ति /
अद्भ्य एवैनम् ओषधीभ्यो ऽध्यवरुन्द्धे //
देवाश् च वा असुराश् चास्पर्धन्त /
ते देवा विजयम् उपयन्तो ऽग्नौ प्रियास् तन्वः संन्यदधत /
यदि जयेमेमा उपावर्तेमहि यदि नो जयेयुर् इमा अभ्युपधावेमेति /
ते ऽभिजित्यान्वैच्छन् सर्वेषां नः सहेति /
सो ऽग्निर् अब्रवीद् यो मा मद्देवत्यम् आदधातै स एताभिस् तनूभिः संभवाद् इति /
तं देवा आदधत /
त एताभिस् तनूभिः समभवन् /
एताभिर् एव तनूभिः संभवति य एवं विद्वान् एतम् आधत्ते /
त्वष्टा पशुकाम आधत्त /
त इमे त्वाष्ट्राः पशवः /
तेनर्द्धाः /
मनुः पुष्टिकाम आधत्त /
स इमान् पोषान् अपुष्यत् /
तेनर्द्धाः /
प्रजापतिः प्रजाकाम आधत्त /
ता इमाः प्राजापत्याः प्रजाः प्राजायन्त /
तेनर्द्धाः /
यो वै तम् आधत्त स तेन वसुना समभवत् /
तस्मात् पुनर्वसुः /
तस्मात् पुनर्वसाव् आधेयः /
आर्ध्नोद् वै स यस् तम् आधत्त /
तस्माद् अनूराधाः /
तस्माद् अनूराधास्व् आधेयः //
text_mt:
The re-establishment [of the fires] is indeed Agni's share.
Desiring to obtain that share, he prospers [him].
If, having established [the fires], he should think, "He is failing," he should re-establish [them].
Which share he prospers, desiring to obtain it, having attained that, he indeed prospers [him].
Everything is made relating to Agni.
Whatever share he has given to Agni, he attains every prosperity.
They say: "The materials are not to be gathered; the Yajus formula is not to be performed.
For his materials have already been gathered, his Yajus formula already performed."
That is not to be heeded.
The materials are indeed to be gathered; the Yajus formula is to be performed.
A restitched garment is to be given, an ox let loose again, a chariot repaired again.
These are the manifestations of the re-establishment.
By their manifestations he makes it flourish.
When Agni departs, he departs following after the waters and plants.
These waters and plants are indeed the darbha grass,
since the clumps of grass are darbha.
From the waters and plants he secures him.
The gods and the asuras contended.
Those gods, going toward victory, deposited their dear bodies in Agni, [saying:]
"If we conquer, we shall return to these; if they conquer us, we shall flee to these."
Having conquered, they sought after [them, saying]: "Together for all of us!"
That Agni said: "Whoever establishes me with me as deity, he shall be united with these bodies."
The gods established him.
They were united with these bodies.
He who, knowing thus, establishes him is united with these very bodies.
Tvaṣṭṛ, desiring cattle, established [him].
These are the cattle of Tvaṣṭṛ;
thereby they prospered.
Manu, desiring nourishment, established [him].
He nourished these nourishments;
thereby he prospered.
Prajāpati, desiring offspring, established [him].
These offspring of Prajāpati were born;
thereby they prospered.
He who established him became united with that good (vasu);
therefore, [the asterism is] Punarvasu.
Therefore, he is to be established under Punarvasu.
He who established him prospered (ārdhnot);
therefore, [the asterism is] Anūrādhās.
Therefore, he is to be established under Anūrādhās.

text_mt:
When Agni departs, he departs following after the year.
Seventeen sāmidhenī verses are to be used.
Five are the seasons; twelve are the months.
This indeed is that year.
From the year itself he extends the opening of the sacrifice.
Regarding that, they say: "Only fifteen are to be used, not seventeen.
For that is more of a transition of the year, namely that there are fifteen."
Fifteen sāmidhenī verses are recited;
fifteen are the nights of a half-month.
By them indeed those are obtained.
As many syllables as the sāmidhenī verses have, so many are the days of the year;
by them indeed those are obtained.
When Agni departs, he departs following after the year.
Six indeed are the seasons, the year.
In that there are six divisions,
from the year itself he secures him.
The year is Agni Vaiśvānara;
six are the seasons.
Therefore, there are six divisions.
In that, being of two syllables, they are made into four syllables;
for up to four are these cattle paired as couples.
In that they distribute this Agni in many ways, in that he nourished these nourishments,
therefore Agni alone attains so many divisions, not any other deity.
The fore-offerings are the opening of the sacrifice.
If he were to omit the fore-offerings, he would omit the opening of the sacrifice.
The fore-offerings are food.
If he were to omit the fore-offerings, he would omit food.
He who should desire, "May I prosper," should make the divisions after the fore-offerings.
The divisions are vigor;
from vigor itself he utters the vaṣaṭ-call.
He quickly approaches prosperity.
They say: "It is made not unrelated to Agni; why do the fore-offerings have divisions?"
In that they are fore-offerings, they are sacrificed around the year.
By that, it is made relating to Agni; by that, it is made not unrelated to Agni.
"Return again with nourishment, return again, O Agni, with refreshment and long life;
protect us again from distress!"
— thus he should offer before the fore-offerings.
"Return with wealth, O Agni; swell with a stream
all-nourishing from every side!"
— thus he should offer after the after-offerings.
Departing, he departs together with nourishment and cattle.
He secures nourishment and cattle again.
Moreover, he prospers with the wish of the sacrifice from both sides.

They say: "It is not made solely for Agni. Why do they sacrifice the two ghee-portions?"
The two eyes of the sacrifice are indeed the two ghee-portions.
If he were to omit the two ghee-portions, he would omit the two eyes of the sacrifice.
He should place the verse: "O Agni, you purify our life-spans" in place of Soma's ghee-portion.
Because it relates to Agni,
therefore it is Agni's.
Because it is Purifying,
therefore it is Soma's.
It is not made solely for Agni;
he does not omit Soma.
He should place the verse: "Agni is the head, the summit of heaven" in place of Soma's ghee-portion, for one desiring offspring or desiring cattle.
Because it forms a pair,
therefore it possesses generation.
Because it has seed,
therefore it is Soma's.
It is not made solely for Agni;
he does not omit Soma.
He who lets the fire go out is indeed a slayer of the heroes of the gods.
A hundred-giver is a hero.
Since these syllables form sets of five containing a hundred syllables,
he thereby redeems a hero of the gods.
For one measure [of life] the fire is to be established; for another, to be re-established.
He does not win by establishing [the fire] that [measure of life] for which it is to be re-established.
Only by the re-establishment [of the fires] does he win it.
Old age is indeed the life-span ordained by the gods;
for so many years does he live.
Therefore they say: "A hundred-giver is a hero."
Since these are syllables forming sets of five containing a hundred syllables,
whatever virility there is, that he obtains, that he wins.
He who lets the fire go out is deprived of life-span and virility.
A hundred-lived is man, of a hundred virilities.
Gold is life-span and virility.
Because he gives gold weighing a hundred measures,
he recovers life-span and virility.

केतः सकेतः सुकेतस् ते न आदित्या जुषाणा अस्य हविषो व्यन्तु स्वाहा /
सलिलः सलिगः सगरस् ते न आदित्या जुषाणा अस्य हविषो व्यन्तु स्वाहा /
दिवो ज्योतिर् विवस्व आदित्य ते नो देवा देवेषु सत्यां देवहूतिम् आसुवध्वम् /
आदित्येभ्यः स्वाहेत्य् एतैर् वै ते तम् आदधत /
यद् एवैतैर् आधत्ते ऽथाहितः /
आदित्यो हि पुनराधेयः //
text_mt:
He who lets the fire go out is deprived of sacrifice and virility.
The sacrifice is fivefold.
Because it [the cake] is on five potsherds,
he takes hold of the sacrifice itself.
Regarding that, they say: "It is only to be on eight potsherds, not on five potsherds.
The gāyatrī has eight syllables.
Agni belongs to the gāyatrī, having the gāyatrī metre.
This which is the re-establishment [of the fires] is made relating to Agni.
Therefore it should be on eight potsherds."
That is not to be heeded.
It is only to be made on five potsherds.
When Agni departs, he departs following after the year.
Five indeed are the seasons, the year.
From the fifth season the sixth season arose.
It is the same thing, that the fifth season and the sixth [are one].
Because it is on five potsherds,
he obtains him from the year itself.
Five are the seasons.
The seasons are generation.
Because it is on five potsherds,
[it is] for generation.
The seasons are generation, Agni is the generator.
Because it is on five potsherds,
the generator generates him from generation itself.
The Ādityas went from here to that world with everything.
They became thirsty.
They realized: "We have come here because of giving from that [world]."
They re-established this [fire].
Thereby they prospered.
The Ādityas are prosperous in this world, the Ādityas in that world.
Cattle are in this world, seasons in that world.
He who knowing thus sacrifices with this [rite] prospers in both worlds.
"Keta, Saketa, Suketa: may you Ādityas, enjoying this oblation, partake of it, svāhā!
Salila, Saliga, Sagara: may you Ādityas, enjoying this oblation, partake of it, svāhā!
Light of heaven, shining one, Āditya: O gods, impel our true invocation of the gods among the gods!
Svāhā to the Ādityas!" — with these [formulas] they established it.
When he establishes it with these, then it is established;
for the re-establishment [of the fires] belongs to the Ādityas.

ओम् //
उद् उ त्वा विश्वे देवास् अग्ने भरन्तु चित्तिभिः /
स नो भव शिवस् त्वं सुप्रतीको विभावसुः //
प्रेद् अग्ने ज्योतिष्मान् याहि शिवेभिर् अर्चिभिष् ट्वम् /
बृहद्भिर् भानुभिर् भासन् मा हिंसीस् तन्वा प्रजाः //
अक्रन्दद् अग्निः //
अन्नपते अन्नस्य नो देह्य् अनमीवस्य शुष्मिणः /
प्रप्र दातारं तारिष ऊर्जं नो धेहि द्विपदे चतुष्पदे //
समिधाग्निं दुवस्यत //
प्रप्रायम् अग्निर् भरतस्य शृण्वे वि यत् सूर्यो न रोचते बृहद् भाः /
अभि यः पूरुं पृतनासु तस्थौ दीदाय दैव्यो अतिथिः शिवो नः //
आपो देवीः प्रतिगृह्णीत भस्मैतत् स्योने कृणुध्वं सुरभाव् उ लोके /
तस्मै नमन्तां जनयः सुपत्नीर् मातेव पुत्रं बिभृता स्योनम् //
अप्स्व् अग्ने सधिष् टव सौषधीर् अनुरुध्यसे /
गर्भे संजायसे पुनः //
गर्भो अस्य् ओषधीनां गर्भो वनस्पतीनाम् /
गर्भो विश्वस्य भूतस्याग्ने गर्भो अपाम् असि //
प्रसद्य भस्मना योनिम् अपश् च पृथिवीम् अग्ने /
संसृज्य मातृभिष् ट्वं ज्योतिष्मान् पुनर् आसदः //
पुनर् आसद्य सदनम् अपश् च पृथिवीम् अग्ने /
शेषे मातुर् यथोपस्थे ऽन्तर् अस्यां शिवतमः //
पुनर् ऊर्जा // सह रय्या //
बोधा मे अस्य वचसो यविष्ठ मंहिष्ठस्य प्रभृतस्य स्वधावः /
पीयति त्वो अनु त्वो गृणाति वन्दारुस् ते तन्वं वन्दे अग्ने //
