meaning:
अथैता आश्विनीः /
उत्सन्नयज्ञो वा एष यद् अग्निः /
को ह तद् वेद यावद् एतस्य न क्रियते यावन् न चीयते /
अश्विनौ देवानां भिषजौ /
यद् एवास्यात्र न क्रियते यन् न चीयते तद् एताभिः कल्पयति तद् भिषज्यति /
पञ्चैता उपदधाति /
पाङ्क्तो ऽग्निः /
यावान् एवाग्निस् तस्मै भेषजं करोति /
अग्नेर् एवैताभिर् दिशः कल्पयते /
अदित्यास् त्वा पृष्ठे सादयामीति /
इमान् एवैतया लोकान् दाधार /
ऋतव्या उपदधाति /
ऋतूनां विधृत्यै /
पञ्चोपदधाति /
पञ्च वा ऋतवः /
यावन्त एवर्तवस् तान् कल्पयति /
समानप्रभृतयो भवन्ति समानोदर्काः /
समानप्रभृतयो ह्य् ऋतवः समानोदर्काः /
एकया व्याहृत्या व्यावर्तयति /
तस्माद् ऋतवो व्यावर्तन्ते /
तस्मात् समानस्य संवत्सरस्य नानारूपाणि /
आश्विनीर् अन्व् ऋतव्या उपदधाति /
रेतस्य् एव हित ऋतून् उपदधाति /
तस्माद् रेतो हितम् ऋतून् अनु प्रजायते /
ऋतव्या अनु वायव्या उपदधाति /
ऋतुष्व् एव प्राणं दधाति /
तस्माद् एते समानाः परियन्तो न जीर्यन्ति /
तस्माद् ऋतून् अनु वायुर् आवरीवर्त्ति /
वायव्या अन्व् अपस्या उपदधाति /
तस्माद् वायुर् वृष्टिं वहति /
वृष्टिम् एवैताभिर् अवरुन्द्धे /
यद् एकधोपदध्याद् एकम् ऋतुं वर्षेत् /
अनुपरिहारं सादयति /
तस्माद् ऋतुमृतुं वर्षति /
अपस्या अनु वयस्या उपदधाति /
पशवो वै वयस्याः /
यद् अप्स्या अनु वयस्या उपदधाति
तस्मान् नानामनसः पशवो नानाव्रता अप एवाभि समनसः /
अपस्या उपधाय वयस्या उपदध्याद् यं कामयेत पशुमान् स्याद् इति /
संज्ञानं वा एतत् पशूनां यद् आपः /
संज्ञान एव पशूनाम् अग्निं चिनुते /
पशुमान् भवति /
वयस्या उपधायापस्या उपदध्याद् यं कामयेतापशुः स्याद् इति /
पशूनाम् एवासंज्ञने ऽग्निं चिनुते /
अपशुर् भवति /
चतस्रः पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति /
तस्मात् पुरस्तात् पशुर् अणीयान् /
तस्मा चत्वारि चक्षुषो रूपाणि द्वे शुक्ले द्वे कृष्णे /
मूर्धन्वतीः /
तस्मात् पुरस्तात् पशूनां मूर्धा /
पञ्चपञ्चाभितः
पशोः सयत्वाय /
तस्मात् प्राङ् पशुः प्रवणः /
बस्तो वय इति दक्षिणत उपदधाति /
वृष्णिर् वय इत्य् उत्तरात् /
अंसाव् एवास्योपदधाति /
व्याघ्रो वय इति दक्षिणे पक्षे /
सिंहो वय इत्य् उत्तरस्मिन् /
पक्षयोर् एव वीर्यं दधाति /
व्याघ्रो वय इति पूर्वाम् /
सिंहो वय इत्य् अपराम् /
तस्मात् पुरो व्याघ्रो जायते पश्चात् सिंहः /
पुरुषो वय इति मध्ये /
तस्मात् पुरुषः पशूनाम् अधिपतिः //

indrāgnī avyathamānām iti /
ojo vai vīryam indrāgnī /
antarikṣam eṣā citiḥ /
śithilam ivāntarikṣam /
prajā antarikṣam /
prajāsv evaujo vīryaṃ dadhāti /
svayamātṛṇṇā bhavati
prāṇānām utsṛṣṭyai svargasya lokasyānukhyātyai /
prājāpatyo 'śvaḥ /

prajāpatinaivainaṃ cinute /
athaitā diśyāḥ /
devānāṃ vai svargaṃ lokaṃ yatāṃ teṣāṃ diśa samavlīyanta /
ta etā diśyā apaśyan /
tābhir diśo 'dṛṃhan /
yad etā upadhīyante

tasmād eṣā diśāṃ virājati /
samrāḍ asi pratīcī dig iti /
tasmād atra sāmrājyam /
svarāḍ asy udīcī dig iti /
tasmād atra svārājyam /
adhipatny asi bṛhatī dig iti
tasmād eṣā diśām adhipatnī /
etāny eva sarvāṇi bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān etā upadhatte /
āyur me pāhīti daśa purastādupadadhāti /
nava vai puruṣe prāṇā nābhir daśamī /

meaning:
इन्द्राग्नी अव्यथमानाम् इति /
ओजो वै वीर्यम् इन्द्राग्नी /
अन्तरिक्षम् एषा चितिः /
शिथिलम् इवान्तरिक्षम् /
प्रजा अन्तरिक्षम् /
प्रजास्व् एवौजो वीर्यं दधाति /
स्वयमातृण्णा भवति
प्राणानाम् उत्सृष्ट्यै स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै /
प्राजापत्यो ऽश्वः /
यद् अश्वम् उपघ्रापयति
प्रजापतिनैवैनं चिनुते /
अथैता दिश्याः /
देवानां वै स्वर्गं लोकं यतां तेषां दिश समव्लीयन्त /
त एता दिश्या अपश्यन् /
ताभिर् दिशो ऽदृंहन् /
यद् एता उपधीयन्ते
दिशां विधृत्यै /
राज्ञ्य् असि प्राची दिग् इति /
तस्माद् एषा दिशां राज्ञी /
विराड् असि दक्षिणा दिग् इति /
तस्माद् एषा दिशां विराजति /
सम्राड् असि प्रतीची दिग् इति /
तस्माद् अत्र साम्राज्यम् /
स्वराड् अस्य् उदीची दिग् इति /
तस्माद् अत्र स्वाराज्यम् /
अधिपत्न्य् असि बृहती दिग् इति
तस्माद् एषा दिशाम् अधिपत्नी /
एतान्य् एव सर्वाणि भवति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
आयुर् मे पाहीति दश पुरस्तादुपदधाति /
नव वै पुरुषे प्राणा नाभिर् दशमी /
प्राणान् एवास्मिन् दधाति /
ज्योतिर् मे यच्छेत्य् उत्तमाम् /
ज्योतिर् एवोत्तमं दधाति /
तस्माद् वाक् प्राणानां ज्योतिर् उत्तमम् /
दशैता उपदधाति /
दशाक्षरा विराट् /
विराट् छन्दसां ज्योतिः /
चक्षुर् ज्योतिः /
चक्षुर् एव प्रजानां पुरस्ताद् दधाति /
मा छन्द इति दक्षिणतः /
तस्माद् दक्षिणावृतो मासाः /
पृथिवी छन्द इति पश्चात्
प्रतिष्ठित्यै /
अग्निर् देवतेत्य् उत्तरात् /
ओजो वा अग्निः /
ओज एवोत्तराद् दधाति /
तस्माद् उत्तराद् अभिप्रयायी जयति /
द्वादश दक्षिणत उपदधाति /
द्वादश पश्चाद्
द्वादशोत्तरात् /
ताः षट्त्रिंशत् संपद्यन्ते /
षट्त्रिंशदक्षरा बृहती /
बृहती छन्दसां स्वाराज्यम् आनशे /
स्वाराज्यं गच्छति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
षट्त्रिंशद् एताः /
षट्त्रिंशदक्षरा बृहती /
बार्हताः पशवः /
अन्तरिक्षम् एषा चितिः /
पशवो ऽन्तरिक्षम् /
पशुष्व् एव पशून् दधाति /
आदित्यधामानो वा अन्ये प्राणा अङ्गिरोधामान्नो ऽन्ये /
ये पुरस्तात् त आदित्यधामानो ये पश्चात् ते ऽङ्गिरोधामानः /
मूर्धासि राड् इति पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति /
य आदित्यधामानः प्राणास् तांस् तद् दाधार /
यन्त्री राड् इति पश्चात् /
ये ऽङ्गिरोधामानः प्राणास् तांस् तद् दाधार /
सप्त पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति सप्त पश्चात् /
तस्माद् अधरः प्राण उत्तरेषां प्राणानाम् अर्धभाक् /
प्रजापतिः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा तासाम् अकामयत मूर्धा स्याम् इति /
स एता मूर्धन्या अपश्यत् /
ताभिर् निरजिहीत /
तासां मूर्धाभवत् /
तन् मूर्धन्यानां मूर्धन्यात्वम् /
मूर्धैव समानानां भवति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते //

sanskrit_iast:

yajñamukhaṃ vai trivṛt /
yajñamukham eva purastād viyātayati /
vyomā saptadaśa iti dakṣiṇataḥ /
annaṃ vai saptadaśaḥ /
saptadaśaṃ vai saṃvatsaram annam anuprajāyate /
annam eva dakṣiṇato dadhāti /
tasmād dakṣiṇena hastena puruṣo 'nnam atti /
yat saptadaśavatīṃ dakṣiṇata upadadhāti
tasmād dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣaṃ vayāṃsy anupariplavante /
ekaviṃśavatīṃ paścāt
pratiṣṭhityai /
paścād dhi vayāṃsi pratitiṣṭhanti /
pañcadaśavatīm uttarāt /
ojo vai pañcadaśaḥ /
oja evottarād dadhāti /
tasmād uttarād abhiprayāyī jayati /
pratūrtir aṣṭādaśa iti purastāt /
dvau trivṛtāv abhipūrvam eva yajñamukhe viyātayati /
pañcadaśavatīṃ dakṣiṇataḥ saptadaśavatīm uttarāt
pakṣayoḥ sayatvāya /
annaṃ vai saptadaśaḥ /
yat saptadaśavatīm ubhayata upadadhāti /
annam evobhayato dadhāti /
tasmād ubhābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ parigṛhya puruṣo 'nnam atti /
ekaviṃśavatīṃ paścāt
pratiṣṭhityai /
agner bhāgo 'si dīkṣāyā ādhipatyaṃ brahma spṛtaṃ trivṛt stoma iti /
etadetad vai devā etābhir aspṛṇvan /
etadetad evaitābhi spṛṇoti /
ta etā spṛtayo nāmeṣṭakāḥ /
ekayāstuvata prajā adhīyanteti /
etadetad vai devā etābhir asṛjanta /
etad evaitābhiḥ sarvam avarunddhe /
arkasya vā eṣā vidhām anuvidhīyate /
annam arko 'rko 'gniḥ /
atty annaṃ yasyaiṣaivaṃ viduṣo vidhīyate //
meaning:
आशुस् त्रिवृद् इति पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति /
यज्ञमुखं वै त्रिवृत् /
यज्ञमुखम् एव पुरस्ताद् वियातयति /
व्योमा सप्तदश इति दक्षिणतः /
अन्नं वै सप्तदशः /
सप्तदशं वै संवत्सरम् अन्नम् अनुप्रजायते /
अन्नम् एव दक्षिणतो दधाति /
तस्माद् दक्षिणेन हस्तेन पुरुषो ऽन्नम् अत्ति /
यत् सप्तदशवतीं दक्षिणत उपदधाति
तस्माद् दक्षिणं पक्षं वयांस्य् अनुपरिप्लवन्ते /
एकविंशवतीं पश्चात्
प्रतिष्ठित्यै /
पश्चाद् धि वयांसि प्रतितिष्ठन्ति /
पञ्चदशवतीम् उत्तरात् /
ओजो वै पञ्चदशः /
ओज एवोत्तराद् दधाति /
तस्माद् उत्तराद् अभिप्रयायी जयति /
प्रतूर्तिर् अष्टादश इति पुरस्तात् /
द्वौ त्रिवृताव् अभिपूर्वम् एव यज्ञमुखे वियातयति /
पञ्चदशवतीं दक्षिणतः सप्तदशवतीम् उत्तरात्
पक्षयोः सयत्वाय /
अन्नं वै सप्तदशः /
यत् सप्तदशवतीम् उभयत उपदधाति /
अन्नम् एवोभयतो दधाति /
तस्माद् उभाभ्यां हस्ताभ्यां परिगृह्य पुरुषो ऽन्नम् अत्ति /
एकविंशवतीं पश्चात्
प्रतिष्ठित्यै /
अग्नेर् भागो ऽसि दीक्षाया आधिपत्यं ब्रह्म स्पृतं त्रिवृत् स्तोम इति /
एतदेतद् वै देवा एताभिर् अस्पृण्वन् /
एतदेतद् एवैताभि स्पृणोति /
त एता स्पृतयो नामेष्टकाः /
एकयास्तुवत प्रजा अधीयन्तेति /
एतदेतद् वै देवा एताभिर् असृजन्त /
एतद् एवैताभिः सर्वम् अवरुन्द्धे /
अर्कस्य वा एषा विधाम् अनुविधीयते /
अन्नम् अर्को ऽर्को ऽग्निः /
अत्त्य् अन्नं यस्यैषैवं विदुषो विधीयते //
text_mt:
With 'The swift one, the trivṛt [stoma],' he lays [a brick] down in front.
The trivṛt is indeed the face of the sacrifice;
he arranges the face of the sacrifice in front.
With 'The expanse, the seventeenfold [stoma],' [he lays a brick down] on the south.
The seventeenfold is indeed food;
along with the year as the seventeenth, food is reproduced;
he places food on the south.
Therefore a man eats food with his right hand.
Because he lays down [a brick] containing the seventeenfold on the south,
therefore birds hover turning toward their right wing.
[He lays down a brick] containing the twenty-onefold in the west,
for stability;
for birds rest upon their rear [parts].
[He lays down a brick] containing the fifteenfold in the north.
The fifteenfold is indeed force;
he places force in the north.
Therefore one advancing from the north conquers.
With 'The speeding one, the eighteenfold [stoma],' [he lays one down] in front.
He arranges two trivṛt [stomas] in proper succession at the face of the sacrifice.
[He lays down a brick] containing the fifteenfold on the south, [and a brick] containing the seventeenfold on the north,
for the coherence of the two wings.
The seventeenfold is indeed food.
Because he lays down [a brick] containing the seventeenfold on both sides,
he places food on both sides.
Therefore, having taken hold [of it] with both hands, a man eats food.
[He lays down a brick] containing the twenty-onefold in the west,
for stability.
With 'You are the share of Agni, the lordship of the consecration, the holy power won, the trivṛt stoma,' [he lays them down].
All this indeed the gods won through these [bricks];
all this indeed he wins through these.
Therefore these bricks are named Spṛt [('winning')] bricks.
With 'With one they praised; creatures were maintained,' [he lays them down].
All this indeed the gods created through these;
all this indeed he secures through these.
This [fire altar] is arranged after the manner of the Arka;
food is the Arka; the Arka is Agni;
he eats food for whom, knowing thus, this is arranged.

प्रतिष्ठित्यै /

text_mt:
The gods and the Asuras did indeed act in the sacrifice equally.
Whatever the gods did, that the Asuras did.
Those gods saw this fourth layer;
having recited it one way, they laid it down another way.
The Asuras did not follow along with that.
Then the gods prevailed, the Asuras were defeated.
For whom, knowing thus, [the layer] is laid down, and who, knowing thus, lays [it] down, he himself prevails, his rival is defeated.
With 'The swift one, the trivṛt [stoma],' he lays [a brick] down in front.
The trivṛt is indeed the face of the sacrifice;
he places the face of the sacrifice in front.
With 'The expanse, the seventeenfold [stoma],' [he lays a brick down] on the south.
The seventeenfold is indeed food;
he secures food on the south.
[He lays down a brick] containing the twenty-onefold in the west,
for stability.
[He lays down a brick] containing the fifteenfold in the north.
The fifteenfold is indeed force;
he places force in the north.
Therefore one advancing from the north conquers. …

sanskrit_iast:
... [ yavānāṃ bhāgo 'sīti dakṣiṇataḥ / ]
[ mā]sā vai yavāḥ /
annaṃ māsāḥ /
annam eva dakṣiṇato 'varunddhe /
ṛbhūṇāṃ bhāgo 'sīti paścāt /
trayastriṃśad devatāḥ /
devatāsv eva pratitiṣṭhati /
vīvarto 'ṣṭācatvāriṃśa ity uttarāt /
tasmād dhastau samāvadvīryau /
arkasya vā eṣā vidhām anuvidhīyate /
annam arko 'rko 'gniḥ /
atty annaṃ yasyaivaṃ viduṣo vidhīyate /
yā mukhyās tāḥ purastād upadadhāti /
āsya mukhyo jāyate ya evaṃ veda /
yā annavatīs tā dakṣiṇataḥ /
āsyānnādo jāyate ya evaṃ veda /
yā pratiṣṭhāvatīs tāḥ paścāt /
gacchati pratiṣṭhāṃ ya evaṃ veda /
yā ojasvatīs tā uttarāt /
āsya balī jāyate ya evaṃ veda /
ya evam etāsāṃ kḷptiṃ veda kalpate 'smai //
meaning:
... [ यवानां भागो ऽसीति दक्षिणतः / ]
[ मा]सा वै यवाः /
अन्नं मासाः /
अन्नम् एव दक्षिणतो ऽवरुन्द्धे /
ऋभूणां भागो ऽसीति पश्चात् /
त्रयस्त्रिंशद् देवताः /
देवतास्व् एव प्रतितिष्ठति /
वीवर्तो ऽष्टाचत्वारिंश इत्य् उत्तरात् /
तस्माद् धस्तौ समावद्वीर्यौ /
अर्कस्य वा एषा विधाम् अनुविधीयते /
अन्नम् अर्को ऽर्को ऽग्निः /
अत्त्य् अन्नं यस्यैवं विदुषो विधीयते /
या मुख्यास् ताः पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति /
आस्य मुख्यो जायते य एवं वेद /
या अन्नवतीस् ता दक्षिणतः /
आस्यान्नादो जायते य एवं वेद /
या प्रतिष्ठावतीस् ताः पश्चात् /
गच्छति प्रतिष्ठां य एवं वेद /
या ओजस्वतीस् ता उत्तरात् /
आस्य बली जायते य एवं वेद /
य एवम् एतासां कॢप्तिं वेद कल्पते ऽस्मै //

agne jātān praṇudā naḥ sapatnān iti purastād upadadhāti /
ya evainaṃ pūrvo 'tikrānto bhrātṛvyas taṃ tayā praṇudate /
sahasā jātān iti paścāt /
ya evainaṃ paścād bhrātṛvyas taṃ tayāpanudate /
ṣoḍaśa stoma ity uttarāt /
catuścatvāriṃśa stoma iti dakṣiṇataḥ /
vajro vai ṣoḍaśaḥ /
vajras triṣṭup /
traiṣṭubhaś catuścatvāriṃśaḥ /
savyāpagrahaṇo vai vajro dakṣiṇāvisarjanaḥ /
bhrātṛvyam eva praṇudya tasmai vajram anuvisṛjati /
catuścatvāriṃśa stoma iti dakṣiṇataḥ /
brahmavarcasaṃ vai catuścatvāriṃśaḥ /
brahmavarcasam eva dakṣiṇato 'varunddhe /
ṣoḍaśa stoma ity uttarāt /
ojo vai ṣoḍaśaḥ /
oja evottarād dadhāti /
tasmād uttarād abhiprayāyī jayati /
pṛthivyāḥ purīṣam asīti madhye /
purīṣaṃ vā ātmano madhyam /
sātmānam evāgniṃ cinute /
tā etā abhrātṛvyā nāmeṣṭakāḥ /
nāsya bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ vidān etā upadhatte /
athaitā virājaḥ /
virājam eva paśuṣūttamāṃ dadhāti /
tasmāt paśumān uttamāṃ vācaṃ vadati /
daśadaśopadadhāti
sayatvāya /
devā vai svargaṃ lokaṃ yantas teṣāṃ yāni cchandāṃsy aniruktāni svargyāṇy āsaṃs taiḥ saha svargaṃ lokam āyan /
tāny ṛṣayo 'nuprājijñāsanta /
tānīṣṭakābhir niramimata /
tānīmāni cchandāṃsi yāny ayajñavāhāni /
yāny eva devānāṃ chandāṃsy aniruktāni svargyāṇi taiḥ saha svargaṃ lokam eti ya evaṃ vidvānetā upadhatte //
athaite stomabhāgāḥ /
bṛhaspatir vā etāṃ yajñasya pratiṣṭhām āharat /

yajñasya pratiṣṭhityai /

satejasam evāgniṃ cinute /

prajananāya /
dakṣiṇato vai devānāṃ yajño 'vlīyata /

saptasaptopadadhāti
savīryatvāya /
trīn madhye
pratiṣṭhityai /
athaitā nākasadaḥ /

svargasya lokasyābhijityai /
na vā amuṃ lokaṃ jagmuṣe kiñca nākam /

yan nākasatsu pañcacūḍā upadadhāti

meaning:
अग्ने जातान् प्रणुदा नः सपत्नान् इति पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति /
य एवैनं पूर्वो ऽतिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्यस् तं तया प्रणुदते /
सहसा जातान् इति पश्चात् /
य एवैनं पश्चाद् भ्रातृव्यस् तं तयापनुदते /
षोडश स्तोम इत्य् उत्तरात् /
चतुश्चत्वारिंश स्तोम इति दक्षिणतः /
वज्रो वै षोडशः /
वज्रस् त्रिष्टुप् /
त्रैष्टुभश् चतुश्चत्वारिंशः /
सव्यापग्रहणो वै वज्रो दक्षिणाविसर्जनः /
भ्रातृव्यम् एव प्रणुद्य तस्मै वज्रम् अनुविसृजति /
चतुश्चत्वारिंश स्तोम इति दक्षिणतः /
ब्रह्मवर्चसं वै चतुश्चत्वारिंशः /
ब्रह्मवर्चसम् एव दक्षिणतो ऽवरुन्द्धे /
षोडश स्तोम इत्य् उत्तरात् /
ओजो वै षोडशः /
ओज एवोत्तराद् दधाति /
तस्माद् उत्तराद् अभिप्रयायी जयति /
पृथिव्याः पुरीषम् असीति मध्ये /
पुरीषं वा आत्मनो मध्यम् /
सात्मानम् एवाग्निं चिनुते /
ता एता अभ्रातृव्या नामेष्टकाः /
नास्य भ्रातृव्यो भवति य एवं विदान् एता उपधत्ते /
अथैता विराजः /
विराजम् एव पशुषूत्तमां दधाति /
तस्मात् पशुमान् उत्तमां वाचं वदति /
दशदशोपदधाति
सयत्वाय /
देवा वै स्वर्गं लोकं यन्तस् तेषां यानि च्छन्दांस्य् अनिरुक्तानि स्वर्ग्याण्य् आसंस् तैः सह स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् /
तान्य् ऋषयो ऽनुप्राजिज्ञासन्त /
तानीष्टकाभिर् निरमिमत /
तानीमानि च्छन्दांसि यान्य् अयज्ञवाहानि /
यान्य् एव देवानां छन्दांस्य् अनिरुक्तानि स्वर्ग्याणि तैः सह स्वर्गं लोकम् एति य एवं विद्वानेता उपधत्ते //
अथैते स्तोमभागाः /
बृहस्पतिर् वा एतां यज्ञस्य प्रतिष्ठाम् आहरत् /
यद् एत उपधीयन्ते
यज्ञस्य प्रतिष्ठित्यै /
बृहस्पतिर् वा एतत् तेजो यज्ञस्य समभरत् /
यद् एत उपधीयन्ते
सतेजसम् एवाग्निं चिनुते /
प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत /
ता स्तोमभागैर् एवासृजत /
यद् एत उपधीयन्ते
प्रजननाय /
दक्षिणतो वै देवानां यज्ञो ऽव्लीयत /
तं स्तोमभागैः प्रत्युदस्तभ्नुवन् /
यद् एते दक्षिणत उदञ्च उपधीयन्ते
यज्ञस्य प्रत्युत्तब्ध्यै /
सप्तसप्तोपदधाति
सवीर्यत्वाय /
त्रीन् मध्ये
प्रतिष्ठित्यै /
अथैता नाकसदः /
नाकसद्भिर् वै देवाः स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् /
यद् एता उपधीयन्ते
स्वर्गस्य लोकस्याभिजित्यै /
न वा अमुं लोकं जग्मुषे किञ्च नाकम् /
तन् नाकसदां नाकसत्त्वम् /
ता एताः सर्वपृष्ठा नामेष्टकाः /
यद् एव किञ्च पृष्ठानां तेजस् तद् अवरुन्द्धे य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
अथैताः पञ्चचूडाः /
यजमानायतनं वै पत्न्यः /
यन् नाकसत्सु पञ्चचूडा उपदधाति
नाक एव यजमानं प्रतिष्ठापयति /
अप्सरसो वा एता एतद् रूपं कृत्वा पत्न्यो भूत्वामुष्मिंल् लोके यजमानम् उपशेरते /
पश्चात् प्राचीम् एकाम् उपदधाति /
तस्मात् पश्चात् प्राची पत्न्य् अन्वास्ते /
तनूपानीर् वा एता यजमानस्य /
सर्वम् आयुर् एति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
एता वै देवताः स्वर्ग्याः /
ताभिर् एव स्वर्गं लोकम् एति /
एता वै देवता अभिचरणीयाः /
यं द्विष्यात् तं ब्रूयाद् अमुं वो जम्भे दधामीति /
एताभ्य एवैनं देवताभ्य आवृश्चति ताजक् प्रधन्वति //
text_mt:
With 'O Agni, thrust away our born rivals,' he lays [a brick] down in front.
Whichever rival has previously surpassed him, him he thrusts away by it.
With 'Those born with force,' in the west.
Whichever rival is behind him, him he thrusts away by it.
With 'The sixteenfold stoma,' on the north.
With 'The forty-fourfold stoma,' on the south.
The thunderbolt is indeed the sixteenfold [stoma];
the thunderbolt is the triṣṭubh;
the forty-fourfold is of triṣṭubh nature.
The thunderbolt is held with the left hand and released toward the south.
Having thrust away the rival, he hurls the thunderbolt after him.
With 'The forty-fourfold stoma,' on the south.
The forty-fourfold is indeed spiritual luster;
he secures spiritual luster on the south.
With 'The sixteenfold stoma,' on the north.
The sixteenfold is indeed force;
he places force on the north.
Therefore one who advances from the north wins.
With 'You are the soil of the earth,' in the middle.
The soil is indeed the middle of the self;
he piles the fire [altar] so as to have a body.
These bricks are indeed called 'rival-less';
he has no rival who, knowing thus, lays these down.
Now these are the virāj [bricks];
he places the virāj as the highest among cattle;
therefore one possessed of cattle speaks the highest speech.
He lays them down by tens
for coherence.
The gods, going to the heavenly world—whichever unexpressed meters of theirs belonged to heaven, with them they went to the heavenly world.
The ṛṣis desired to know them in turn;
they fashioned them with bricks.
These are those meters that do not carry the sacrifice.
Whichever unexpressed meters of the gods belong to heaven, with them he goes to the heavenly world who, knowing thus, lays these down.
Now these are the stomabhāga [bricks];
Bṛhaspati indeed brought this support of the sacrifice.
That these are laid down
is for the supporting of the sacrifice.
Bṛhaspati indeed gathered this fiery energy of the sacrifice.
That these are laid down,
he piles the fire [altar] along with fiery energy.
Prajāpati created creatures;
he created them with the stomabhāgas.
That these are laid down
is for procreation.
The sacrifice of the gods collapsed on the south;
they propped it up with the stomabhāgas.
That these are laid down on the south facing north
is for the propping up of the sacrifice.
He lays them down by sevens
for possessing vigor;
three in the middle
for support.
Now these are the nākasad [bricks];
with the nākasads the gods went to the heavenly world.
That these are laid down
is for conquering the heavenly world.
Indeed, nothing is painful for one who has gone to that world;
that is the nākasad-nature of the nākasads.
These bricks are called 'all-pṛṣṭha';
whatever fiery energy of the pṛṣṭhas there is, that he secures who, knowing thus, lays these down.
Now these are the pañcacūḍā [bricks];
the wives are the domain of the sacrificer;
when he lays down the pañcacūḍās upon the nākasads,
he establishes the sacrificer in the firmament.
These Apsarases indeed, having assumed this form and become wives, lie beside the sacrificer in yonder world.
In the west he lays down one facing east;
therefore in the west the wife sits facing east.
These are body-protectors of the sacrificer;
he reaches full lifespan who, knowing thus, lays these down.
These deities belong to heaven;
with them he goes to the heavenly world.
These deities are for sorcery;
whomever he hates, of him he should say: 'I place such-and-such into your jaws.'
He cuts him off from these deities; quickly he perishes.

yad evāsyātra na kriyate yan na cīyate tad vācā kalpayati tad bhiṣajyati //
meaning:
आयोस् त्वा सदने सादयामीति /
आयुर् एवोत्तमं दधाति /
तस्माद् आयुः प्राणानाम् उत्तमम् /
स्वयमातृण्णा भवति
प्राणानामुत् सृष्ट्यै स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै /
प्राजापत्यो ऽश्वः /
यद् अश्वम् उपघ्रापयति
प्रजापतिनैवैनं चिनुते /
अथैषा विकर्णी /
देवानां वा एषा विक्रान्तिर् यद् विकर्णी /
देवानाम् एवैनं विक्रान्तिम् अनु विक्रमयति /
वायुमती /
प्राणो वै वायुः /
आयुः स्वयमातृण्णा /
आयुश् चैवास्मिन् प्राणं च समीची दधाति /
सं वा एनम् एतद् इन्द्धे यच् चिनोति /
दीपयति वायुमत्या /
संवत्सरम् एवाग्निं चिन्वीत /
संवत्सरो वा अग्निर् वैश्वानरः /
तस्याहोरात्राणीष्टकाः /
आप्तेष्टकम् एवैनं चिनुते /
ऋध्नोति /
यन् नैवं चिन्वीत प्रिययैनं तन्वा व्यर्धयेत् /
यद् एवं चिनुते प्रिययैवैनं तन्वा समर्धयति /
सतनूर् एवैतद् वैश्वानरश् चीयते /
ऋतव्या उपदधाति /
ऋतूनां विधृत्यै /
द्वेद्वे उपदधाति /
द्वौद्वौ ह्य् ऋतवः /
चतस्रो मध्यमायां चित्याम् उपदधाति /
अन्तरिक्षम् इव वा एषा मध्यमा चितिः /
शिथिलम् इवान्तरिक्षम् /
चतस्रो दिशः /
दिक्ष्व् एव प्रतितिष्ठति /
ऋतुभ्यो वा एता देवा निरमिमत /
तद् ऋतव्यानाम् ऋतव्यात्वम् /
आयन्तमायन्तम् ऋतुं प्रतितिष्ठति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
नानाप्रभृतयो भवन्ति समानोदर्काः /
तस्मात् समानस्य संवत्सरस्य नानारूपाणि /
अवकाम् उपदधायेष्टकाम् उपदधाति /
अग्नेर् वा एषा वैश्वानरस्य योनिर् यद् अवका /
स्व एवैना योनाव् उपदधाति /
शान्त्या अनिर्दाहाय /
ऋध्नोति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
अथैता विश्वज्योतिषः /
प्राणभृतो वा एता यजमानस्य /
प्राणम् एव प्रथमया दाधार व्यानं द्वितीययापानं तृतीयया /
एता वै देवताः स्वर्ग्याः /
ताभिर् एव स्वर्गं लोकम् एति /
एता वै देवता ज्योतिष्मतीः /
अग्निर् एवास्मा अस्मिंल् लोके ज्योतिर् भवति वायुर् अन्तरिक्षे सूर्यो दिवि /
सर्वे ऽस्मा इमे लोका ज्योतिष्मन्तो भवन्ति /
अधिपतिवतीर् भवन्ति /
आधिपत्यम् एवैताभिर् गच्छति /
लोकं पृण च्छिद्रं पृणाथो सीद ध्रुवा त्वम् /
इन्द्राग्नी त्वा बृहस्पतिर् इति /
ओजो वै वीर्यम् इन्द्राग्नी /
ओजसैवैनं वीर्येण चिनुते /
ता अस्य सूददोहस इति /
तस्मात् परुषिपरुषि सूदः /
सोमं श्रीणन्ति पृश्नय इति /
अन्नं पृश्नि /
अन्नम् एवावरुन्द्धे /
त्रिष्व् आ रोचने दिव इति /
त्रीणि सवनानि /
सवनेष्व् एवैनं चिनुते /
अनुष्टुब् अनुचरा भवति /
प्राणो वा अनुष्टुप् /
तस्मात् प्राणः सर्वाण्य् अङ्गान्य् अनुसंचरति /
वाग् वा अनुष्टुप् /
यद् एवास्यात्र न क्रियते यन् न चीयते तद् वाचा कल्पयति तद् भिषज्यति //

meaning:
या आग्नेयीर् गायत्रीर् मूर्धन्वतीस् ताभिस् तिसृभिस् तिस्रः पूर्वार्ध उपदध्यात् /
अथ त्रिष्टुब्भिर् अथ जगतीभिर् अथानुष्टुब्भिर् अथ पङ्क्तिभिर् अथ यत् किञ्चाग्नेयं छन्दः /
तिस्र एकेन च्छन्दसा तिस्र एकेन /
सर्वम् अग्निम् अनूपदध्यात् /
एतां ह वै यज्ञसेनश् चैत्रश् चितिं विदांचकार /
तया ह वै स आनर्ध /
ऋध्नोति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
पशवो वै छन्दांसि वामं देवानाम् /
पशून् एव वामं भ्रातृव्यस्य वृङ्क्ते /
आत्मा वा आहवनीयो भ्रातृव्यो धिष्ण्यः /
यद् गार्हपत्य उपदध्याद् भ्रातृव्ये वामं पशून् दध्यात् /
आहवनीय उपदधाति /
आत्मन्न् एव वामं पशून् धत्ते /
सैषोत्तरवेदिर् नाम चितिः
तस्माद् एता उत्तमायां चित्याम् उपधीयन्ते /
उत्तमः समानानां भवति य एवं विद्वान् एता उपधत्ते /
पशुर् वा अग्निः /
अग्निमुखान् प्रजापतिः पशून् असृजत /
यत् पञ्च चितयस्
तस्मात् पाङ्क्ताः पशव उच्यन्ते /
यत् तिस्रश् चितयस्
त्रिवृद् ध्य् अग्निः /
यद् द्वे
द्विपाद् यजमानः /
प्रतिष्ठित्यै /
द्व्यक्षरं लोम द्व्यक्षरं चर्म द्व्यक्षरं मांसं द्व्यक्षरम् अस्थि द्व्यक्षरो मज्जा /
तद् दश /
दशाक्षरा विराट् /
तस्माद् वैराजाः पशव उच्यन्ते //
यो जानुदघ्नः स गायत्रचिद् यो नाभिदघ्नः स त्रिष्टुप्चिद् यः पुरुषमात्रः स जगच्चित् /
श्येनचितं पक्षिणं चिन्वीत स्वर्गकामः /
श्येनो वै वयसां क्षेपिष्ठः /
स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै /
अलजचितं पक्षिणं चिन्वीत प्रतिष्ठाकामः /
चतस्रो दिशः /
दिक्ष्वेव प्रतितिष्ठति /
कङ्कचितं शीर्षण्वन्तं चिन्वीत यः कामयेत सशीर्षामुष्मिंल् लोके स्याम् इति /
सशीर्षैवामुष्मिंल् लोके भवति /
प्रौगचितं चिन्वीत यदि मन्येत पूर्वो मातिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्य इति /
प्रौगचिता वै देवा असुरान् प्राणुदन्त य एनान् पूर्वे ऽतिक्रान्ता आसन् /
य एवैनं पूर्वो ऽतिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्यस् तं तेन प्रणुदते /
उभयतः प्रौगं चिन्वीत यदि मन्येत पश्चान् मे भ्रातृव्य इति /
य एवास्य पश्चाद् भ्रातृव्यस् तं तेनापनुदते प्र श्रेयांसं भ्रातृव्यं नुदते प्रति पापीयांसं नुदते /
रथचक्रचितं चिन्वीताभिचरन् /
रथचक्रचितं ह स्म वै देवा असुरेभ्यो वज्रम् इयद्भ्यस् त्वेत्य् अभ्यवसृजन्ति /
वज्रम् एव भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति स्तृणुत एनम् /
समूह्यं चिन्वीत पशुकामः /
पशवो वै पुरीषम् /
पशून् एवावरुन्द्धे /
परिचाय्यं चिन्वीत सजातकामः परीव वै सजाता विशन्ति /
सजातैर् एवैनं परिचिनोति /
द्रोणचितं चिन्वीतान्नकामः /
पात्रेण वा अन्नम् अद्यते /
तेनैव मुखेनान्नम् अत्ति /
श्मशानचितं चिन्वीत यः कामयेत पितृलोक ऋध्नुयाम् इति /
श्मशानचिता वै यमो ऽमुष्मिंल् लोक आर्ध्नोत् /
पितृलोक एवर्ध्नोति /
गायत्रचितं पक्षिणं चिन्वीत स्वर्गकामः /
अग्निर् वै तत् पक्षी भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपतत् /
यद् आहुर् गायत्री पक्षिणी भूत्वा स्वर्गं लोकम् अपतद् इति
स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै /
ऊर्ध्वा वा अन्ये ऽग्नयश् चीयन्ते न्यञ्चो ऽन्ये /
य ऊर्ध्वाश् चीयन्ते ते ऽमुष्मै लोकाय ये न्यञ्चस्ते ऽस्मै /
यद् ऊर्ध्वस् तिष्ठन् हिरण्यशल्कैः प्रोक्षति
तेनैवोर्ध्वं चिनुते /
स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य समष्ट्यै //

चतुर्विम्̐शतिं रात्रीर् दीक्षितः स्यात् /
चतुर्विंशतिः संवत्सरस्यार्धमासाः /
अर्धमासशः संवत्सर आप्यते /
संवत्सरो विराट्
विराजम् एवाप्नोति /
मासं दीक्षितः स्यात् /
यो मासः स संवत्सरः /
संवत्सरो विराट् /
विराजम् एवाप्नोति /
चतुरो मासो दीक्षितः स्यात् /
चतुरो वा एतं मासौ वसवो ऽबिभरुः /
ते पृथिवीम् आजयन् गायत्रीं छन्दः /
अष्टौ रुद्राः /
ते ऽन्तरिक्षम् आज्यंस् त्रिष्टुभं छन्दः /
द्वादशादित्याः /
ते दिवम् आज्यञ् जगतीं छन्दः /
ततो वै ते व्यावृतम् अगच्छञ् श्रैष्ठ्यं देवानाम् /
द्वादश मासो भृत्वाग्निं चिन्वीत /
द्वादश मासाः संवत्सरः /
तस्याहोरात्राणीष्टकाः /
आप्तेष्टकम् एवैनं चिनुते /
ऋध्नोति /
व्यावृतम् एव गच्छति श्रैष्ठ्यं समानानाम् //
गायत्रं पुरस्ताद् गायति /
शिरो वै देवानां गायत्रम् /
गायत्रो ऽग्निः /
तस्माद् गायत्रं पुरस्ताद् गायत्य् आग्निपावमान्याम् /
अयं वाव यः पवते स प्राणः /
मुखं देवानाम् अग्निः /
मुखत एव प्राणं दधाति /
तस्मान् मुखतः प्राणः /
रथन्तरम् उत्तराद् गायति बृहद् दक्षिणतः /
पक्षाव् एवास्योपदधाति /
इयं वै रथन्तरम् असौ बृहत् /
आभ्याम् एवैनं परिगृह्णाति /
यज्ञायज्ञियं पुच्छे गायति श्रोण्यां वामदेव्यम् /
आत्मा वै यज्ञायज्ञियं तनूर् वामदेव्यम् /
सात्मानम् एवैनं सतनूं चिनुते /
हृदयम् अपिकक्षे /
तस्माद् अपिकक्षे हृदयम् अनृचं भवति /
तस्माद् अनस्थकं हृदयम् /
अर्क्यैः परिगायति /
अर्को वा अग्निः /
अर्कम् एवार्क्यैः परिगायति
शान्त्यै //
text_mt:
The Virāj is to be attained by the initiation.
He should be initiated for three nights.
The Virāj has three feet.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for six nights.
The seasons are six, [namely] the year.
The year is the Virāj.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for ten nights.
The Virāj has ten syllables.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for twelve nights.
The year has twelve months.
The year is the Virāj.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for thirteen nights.
The year has thirteen months.
The year is the Virāj.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for fifteen nights.
Fifteen are the nights of a half-month.
The year is attained half-month by half-month.
The year is the Virāj.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for twenty-four nights.
Twenty-four are the half-months of the year.
The year is attained half-month by half-month.
The year is the Virāj.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for a month.
What is a month is the year.
The year is the Virāj.
He attains the Virāj itself.
He should be initiated for four months.
For four months indeed the Vasus carried him.
They conquered the earth, [and] the gāyatrī meter.
For eight [months] the Rudras [carried him].
They conquered the atmosphere, [and] the triṣṭubh meter.
For twelve [months] the Ādityas [carried him].
They conquered heaven, [and] the jagatī meter.
Then indeed they attained distinction, the supremacy among the gods.
Having carried [him] for twelve months, he should pile the fire [altar].
The year has twelve months.
Its bricks are the days and nights.
He piles him with bricks attained.
He prospers.
He attains distinction, supremacy among his equals.
He sings the Gāyatra [sāman] in front.
The Gāyatra is indeed the head of the gods.
Agni is of gāyatra nature.
Therefore he sings the Gāyatra in front on a verse to Agni Pavamāna.
This breath is indeed that which purifies.
Agni is the mouth of the gods.
He places breath right in the mouth.
Therefore breath is in the mouth.
He sings the Rathantara on the north, the Bṛhat on the south.
He lays down his two wings.
This [earth] is the Rathantara, that [sky] is the Bṛhat.
By these two he encloses him.
He sings the Yajñāyajñīya on the tail, the Vāmadevya on the hip.
The Yajñāyajñīya is the self; the Vāmadevya is the body.
He piles him possessed of a self, possessed of a body.
The Hṛdaya [sāman] is in the armpit.
Therefore the heart is in the armpit; it is without a verse.
Therefore the heart is boneless.
He sings around with the Arka [chants].
Agni is indeed the Arka.
He sings around the Arka with the Arka [chants]
for appeasement.

संवत्सरो वा अन्तरा तमः स्वर्गं लोकम् /
ज्योतिष्मतीर् एताः साहस्रीर् इष्टकाः /
यद् धिरण्यशल्कैः प्रोक्षति
ज्योतिषैवास्मै संवत्सरं विवासयति /
सहस्रस्य प्रमासि सहस्रस्य प्रतिमासीति /
सहस्रस्ंमिता हीमे लोकाः /
घ्नन्ति वा एतद् अग्नेर् यद् अस्यात्र न क्रियते यन् न चीयते /
अमृतं हिरण्यम् /
यद् धिरण्यशल्कैः प्रोक्षति /
अमृतेनैवास्य तन्वं पृणक्ति /
रुद्रं वै देवान् निरभजन् /
स देवान् आयतयाभिपर्यावर्तत /
ते देवा एतच् छतरुद्रियम् अपश्यन् /
तेनैनम् अशमयन् /
यच् छतरुद्रियं जुहोति
तेनैवैनं शमयति /
जानुदघ्ने ऽग्रे जुहोति /
अस्या एव रुद्रम् अवयजते /
अथ नाभिदघ्ने /
अन्तरिक्षाद् एव रुद्रम् अवयजते /
अथ पुरुषमात्रे /
अमुष्या एव रुद्रम् अवयजते /
इत एवोर्ध्वं रुद्रम् अवयजते /
अथ पुरुषमात्रे ऽथ नाभिदघ्ने ऽथ जानुदघ्ने /
अमुत एवार्वाञ्चं रुद्रम् अवयजते /
तत् षट् संपद्यते /
षड् वा ऋतवः /
ऋतुभ्य एव रुद्रं निरवयजते /
गवेधुकासक्तुभिर् वा जर्तिलैर् वा कुसयसर्पिषा वा मृगक्षीरेण वा जुहोति /
यद् ग्राम्येण जुहुयाद् ग्रामावतारिणं रुद्रं कुर्यात् /
आरण्येनैवारण्यम् अभि रुद्रं निरवयजते /
अर्कपर्णेन जुहोति /
अर्को वा अग्निः /

पशुर् वा अग्निः /
एतर्हि वा एष जायते यर्हि चीयते /

text_mt:
The year is indeed the darkness between [here and] the heavenly world.
These bricks belonging to the thousand are luminous.
When he sprinkles with gold flakes,
he illumines the year for him with light.
With 'You are the measure of a thousand, you are the counterpart of a thousand,' [he sprinkles],
for these worlds are commensurate with a thousand.
They kill that of Agni which is not performed here, which is not piled.
Gold is immortal life.
When he sprinkles with gold flakes,
he unites his body with immortal life.
The gods excluded Rudra from sharing.
With drawn bow he turned against the gods.
The gods saw this Śatarudriya [hymn].
With it they appeased him.
When he offers the Śatarudriya,
with it he appeases him.
First he offers at knee-height.
From this [earth] he appeases Rudra.
Then at navel-height.
From the atmosphere he appeases Rudra.
Then at a man's height.
From that [heaven] he appeases Rudra.
From here upward he appeases Rudra.
Then at a man's height, then at navel-height, then at knee-height.
From there downward he appeases Rudra.
That amounts to six.
The seasons are six.
From the seasons he appeases Rudra.
He offers with gavedhukā groats, or with wild sesame, or with butter from a kusaya, or with milk of a wild animal.
If he were to offer with cultivated [substance], he would bring Rudra down into the village.
With wild [substance] he appeases Rudra towards the wilderness.
He offers with an arka leaf.
Agni is indeed the arka.
With the arka he appeases him from the arka.
On the last brick of the northern wing, on that he offers.
This is indeed the quarter of Rudra.
Having turned Rudra toward his own quarter, he appeases him.
Agni is cattle.
He is born at this time when he is piled.
Just as a newborn calf desires to obtain the teat, so indeed does he at this time desire to obtain a portion.
He contemplates both the sacrificer and the Adhvaryu.
When he offers the Śatarudriya,
with a portion he appeases him.
The Aṅgirases, going to the heavenly world, poured out the cauldron on a she-goat.
She, burning, touched a leaf.
That became the arka plant.
That is the arka-nature of the arka.
That he offers with an arka leaf
is for having the same origin.
He should place [the offering-leaf] on the path of the cattle of him whom he hates.
Whichever beast first steps on it, that one incurs affliction.
Those [verses] which are the last, those he should make the sacrificer recite.
These deities are leading to heaven.
By them he goes to the heavenly world.
These deities are to be employed for sorcery.
Him whom he hates, he should say concerning him: 'I place that one in your jaws.'
From these deities he cuts him off; swiftly he perishes.

[With 'United is the abda with the āyus,' [he offers]. / The abda is the year. / The āyus are the months. / The aruṇī is the dawn. / The sūra is] Etaśa. / These two are the Aśvins. / The fire Vaiśvānara is the year. / Iḍā is cattle. / Ghee is cattle. / Cattle are born after the year. / From the year he produces cattle for him. / He offers on a clump of darbha grass. / Whatever un-touched [power], whatever vigor belongs to it, that creeps forth. / Whatever un-touched [power], whatever vigor belongs to it, that he secures. / One who has piled the fire [altar] does not die, for whom they offer thus. / With 'The bright countenance of the gods has arisen' he offers on the human head. / Mitra is day, Varuṇa is night. / Just this much indeed exists. / As much as exists, that he secures. / He offers with a verse to Sūrya. / Therefore only the human among cattle faces Sūrya; the others face downward. / Because he offers twice with the same verse, / therefore the same human has two feet. / Whoever indeed does not yoke the fire when yoking-time comes does not yoke among those who yoke. / 'Yoke indeed, you best summoner of gods,'
and 'Agni, yoke indeed those that are yours,' [he says]. / He yokes the fire itself when yoking-time comes. / He yokes among those who yoke who knows thus. / He yokes with two [verses]. / 'Not singly harnessed,' he says. / Whoever indeed does not unyoke the fire when unyoking-time comes does not unyoke among those who unyoke. / 'As a mother her son, the earth-bearing pan has carried fire in its own lap. / May the All-Gods in agreement with the seasons, may Prajāpati Viśvakarman unyoke it,'
[he says]. / He unyokes the fire itself when unyoking-time comes. / He unyokes among those who unyoke who knows thus. / Now these are the Saṃyānī [bricks]. / These deities indeed lead to heaven. / By means of them he goes to the heavenly world. / This is the Gāyatrī having light as wings. / By means of it he goes to the heavenly world who knows thus. / Just as one traverses by boat from water to water, so indeed the fire-piler traverses yonder in accordance with the world by means of these. / That is why the Saṃyānī [bricks] are called Saṃyānī. / These deities indeed lead to heaven. / By means of them he goes to the heavenly world. / Now these are names of the seasons. / He secures the seasons themselves. / 'Sumeka,' [he says]. / The year is indeed sumeka. / He secures the year itself. / Now these are the Āditya-bricks. / The Ādityas take away the fiery energy of him who, having piled the fire, does not shine, as it were. / When these are laid down, / just as one adds more to a blazing [fire], in the same way he places fiery energy in it in proper succession. / The Ādityas do not take away his fiery energy. / As that [sun] is among the gods, so he becomes among men. / Now these are the ghee-bricks. / Fiery energy is fire, fiery energy is ghee. / He places fiery energy in fiery energy itself. / Now these are the rain-winning [bricks]. / He secures rain by means of them. / By means of them it rains at will yonder for the fire-piler. / That is why the rain-winning [bricks] are called rain-winning. / Now these are the body. / This indeed Śaṅkha Krauṣya said to his son who had piled the fire: / 'Did you pile the fire?' / 'I piled it indeed,' [he said]. / 'Then why have you not attained [heaven] with your whole body?' / 'Because of course we did not know that,' [he said]. / For whom these are laid down, he piles the fire with a body. / They are [bricks] pierced again. / He connects breath in breath itself. / Now this is the sixth layer. / If one who has piled the fire should not establish himself, as it were, he should lay down this sixth layer. / The seasons are six, [namely] the year. / He establishes himself in the seasons, in the year. / These deities indeed lead to heaven. / By means of them he goes to the heavenly world. / These deities are to be used for sorcery. / Whom he hates, of him he should say, 'I place that one in your jaws.' / From these deities he cuts him off; instantly he perishes.

meaning:
अग्निना वै देवाः स्वर्गं लोकम् आयन् /
तान् पराच आवृत्तान् पश्चाद् अन्ववेत्य रक्षांस्य् अजिघांसन् /
ते देवा एता वितृण्णीर् अपश्यन् /
ताभी रक्षांस्य् अपाघ्नत /
यद् द्वे पुरस्ताद् उपदधाति द्वे पश्चात् /
चक्षुर् एवोभयतो दधाति
रक्षसामपहत्यै /
स्वयमातृण्णा भवन्ति
प्राणानाम् उत्सृष्ट्यै स्वर्गस्य लोकस्यानुख्यात्यै /
चतस्रः /
तस्माच् चत्वारि चक्षुषो रूपाणि द्वे शुक्ले द्वे कृष्णे /
स्वर्गाय वै लोकायाग्निश् चीयते /
यद् एकादशिनीं कुर्याद् वज्रेण पुरस्ताद् अवगृह्णीयाद् अस्वर्ग्यः स्यात् /
यद् अनेकादशिनीम् अनवरुद्धा अस्य पशवः स्युः /
एकयूप एकादश पशून् आलभेत /
तेनैव स्वर्ग्यस् तेन पशून् अवरुन्द्धे //
न पक्षसंमितां मिनुयात् /
यत् पक्षसंमितां मिनुयात् कनीयांसं यज्ञक्रतुम् उपेयात् पापीयस्यस्य प्रजात्मनः स्यात् /
वेदिसंमितां मिनुयात् /
ज्यायांसम् एव यज्ञक्रतुम् उपैति नास्यात्मनः प्रजा पापीयसी भवति /

कस्मै कम् अग्निश् चीयत इत्य् आहुः /
अन्नम् अदानि गृहा मे ऽसन्न् इति वा अग्निश् चीयते /
य एवं विद्वान् अग्निं चिनुते ऽत्त्य् अन्नं गृहवान् भवति //
सहस्रेष्टकं चिन्वीत प्रथमं चिन्वानः /
सहस्रसंमितो ह्य् अयं लोकः /
द्वे सहस्रे द्वितीयं चिन्वानः /
अन्तरिक्षेण संमितम् /
त्रीणि सहस्राणि तृतीयं चिन्वानः /

व्रतं चरेद् अग्निं [ चित्वा / ]

[ द्वितीयं चित्वा नान्येषां स्त्रियः / ]
[ तृतीयं चित्वा न कांचन / ]
[ रेतो वा एतन् निधत्ते यद् अग्निं ] चिनुते /
यद् उपेयाद् रेतसा व्यृध्येत /
तद् आहुर् ये एवामू रेत सिचाव् इष्टके ते अग्निचितो रेतो बिभृतः /
तस्माद् उपेत्यैति /
प्रजापतिर् वा उख्यम् आग्नम् अबिभः /
स इमाः प्रजा अनुप्राविशत् /
सो ऽब्रवीत् स एव मे प्रजानाम् ऋध्नवद् यो मेतः संचिनवद् इति /
अग्निः प्रजापतिः /
यद् अग्निं चिनुते प्रजापतिम् एव संचिनोति /
ऋध्नोति /
तच् चित्यस्य चित्यत्वम् /
तं वसुभ्यः प्रायच्छत् /
तेन वसवस् त्रीणि च शतानि त्रयस्त्रिंशतं चासृजन्त /
ते वसवो रुद्रेभ्यः प्रायच्छन् /
तेन रुद्रास् त्रीणि च शतानि त्रयस्त्रिंशतं चासृजन्त /
तं रुद्रा आदित्येभ्यः प्रायच्छन् /
तेनादित्यास् त्रीणि च शतानि त्रयस्त्रिंशतं चासृजन्त /
उखा सहस्रतमी /
य एवं वेदोखां सहस्रतमीं गच्छति साहस्रीं पुष्टिं पशूनाम् //
text_mt: By means of the fire the gods went to the heavenly world. / As they turned away, the demons, following from behind, wished to slay them. / The gods saw these perforated [bricks]. / With them they struck away the demons. / That he places two in front and two behind, / he thereby places sight on both sides / for the smiting away of the demons. / They are naturally perforated, / for the release of the vital breaths, for the survey of the heavenly world. / There are four. / Therefore sight has four forms: two white, two black. / For the heavenly world indeed is the fire piled. / If he were to make an [altar-piling with an] elevenfold set [of posts], he would obstruct it from the front with the thunderbolt; it would not lead to heaven. / If he were not to make an elevenfold set, cattle would not be secured for him. / On a single sacrificial post he should seize eleven victims. / By that very [means] it leads to heaven; by that he secures cattle. // He should not measure [it] out commensurate with the wings. / If he were to measure it out commensurate with the wings, he would undertake an inferior sacrificial performance; his offspring would be worse than himself. / He should measure it out commensurate with the altar. / He undertakes a superior sacrificial performance; his offspring does not become worse than himself. / This indeed Divājāta Śākāyanya said, having heard that Śaṅkha Kauṣya had measured out an elevenfold set commensurate with the wings: 'He has undertaken an inferior sacrificial performance; his offspring will be worse than himself.' / Thence indeed they consider him ruined. / 'For what purpose is the fire piled?' they say. / 'May the gods know me'—for this the fire is piled. / Whoever knowing thus piles this one, the gods know him. / 'For what purpose is the fire piled?' they say. / 'May I eat food, may there be houses for me'—for this the fire is piled. / Whoever knowing thus piles the fire, eats food, becomes possessed of houses. // One who piles [it] for the first time should pile [an altar of] a thousand bricks. / For this world is commensurate with a thousand. / Piling for the second time, [he should pile an altar of] two thousand [bricks], / commensurate with the intermediate space. / Piling for the third time, [he should pile an altar of] three thousand [bricks], / commensurate with these worlds. / Having piled the fire, he should observe a vow: / [having piled it for the first time, he should not approach a dark woman;] / [having piled it for the second time, not the women of others;] / [having piled it for the third time, not any [woman].] / [Semen indeed he deposits when he] piles [the fire]. / If he were to approach [a woman], he would be deprived of semen. / Regarding this they say: 'Those two seed-pourer bricks, they bear the semen of the fire-piler.' / Therefore he may approach [a woman]. / Prajāpati indeed carried the fire in the pan. / He entered into these creatures. / He said: 'Only he among my creatures shall prosper who shall gather me together from here.' / Agni is Prajāpati. / When he piles the fire, he gathers together Prajāpati himself. / He prospers. / That is the pile-nature of the piled [fire]. / He gave it to the Vasus. / With it the Vasus produced three hundred and thirty-three. / The Vasus gave it to the Rudras. / With it the Rudras produced three hundred and thirty-three. / The Rudras gave it to the Ādityas. / With it the Ādityas produced three hundred and thirty-three. / The pan is the thousandth. / Whoever thus knows the pan as the thousandth attains the thousandfold nourishment of cattle.

meaning:
यथारूपम् अग्निश् चेतव्यः /
यो वै यथारूपम् अग्निं चिनुते नास्यापरूपम् आत्मञ् जायते /
गायत्र्या प्रथमां चितिं संचिताम् अभिमृशेत् त्रि[ष्टुभा द्वितीयां जगत्या तृतीयाम् अ]नुष्टुभा चतुर्थीं पङ्क्त्या पञ्चमीम् /
यथारूपम् एवाग्निं चिनुते /
नास्यापरूपम् आत्मञ् जायते /
प्राणो वै प्रथमा चितिर् व्यानो द्वितीयापानस् तृतीया /
प्राणापानैर् एवैनं समिन्द्धे /
इडाया वा एषा विभक्तिः /
पशव इडा /
पशुभिर् एवैनं चिनुते /

अश्वाव् अभितस् तिष्ठेतां श्याव उत्तराच् छ्वेतो दक्षिणतः /

प्राजापत्यो ऽश्वः /

हिरण्यपात्रं मधोः पूर्णं ब्रह्मणे ददाति /
मधव्यो भवति /
शतमानम् /

चित्रं देवानाम् इति / चित्रवत्यावेक्षते /

तत् पञ्च संपद्यते /

कस्यै देवताया अग्निश् चीयत इत्य् आहुर् ब्रह्मवादिनः /
प्रजापतय एव /
तस्य किं हविर् इति /
आत्मैव //
text_mt: The fire is to be piled according to its proper form. / Whoever piles the fire according to its proper form, in him no deformity is born. / With the gāyatrī he should touch the first layer when piled; with the triṣṭubh the second; with the jagatī the third; with the anuṣṭubh the fourth; with the paṅkti the fifth. / He piles the fire according to its proper form. / In him no deformity is born. / The out-breath is the first layer, the inter-breath the second, the in-breath the third. / With the out- and in-breaths he kindles it. / This is the division of Iḍā. / Iḍā is cattle. / With cattle he piles it. / Having announced it to Prajāpati, the fire is to be piled. / Whoever piles the fire without having announced it to Prajāpati incurs misfortune. / Two horses should stand on either side: a dark-brown one to the north, a white one to the south. / Touching them, he should place brick after brick. / This is the form of Prajāpati. / The horse belongs to Prajāpati. / Having announced it to Prajāpati, he piles the fire; he does not incur misfortune. // He gives a golden vessel full of honey to the Brahman. / He becomes possessed of honey. / [It is] of a hundred measures. / Man has a lifespan of a hundred [years], a hundredfold vigor. / Lifespan and vigor he places in himself. / With 'A marvelous [face of the gods has arisen],' with [a verse] containing the word 'marvelous' (citra), he gazes [upon it]. / It becomes marvelous at midday. / He makes the horse sniff [the fire]. / Yonder sun is Indra, this is Prajāpati. / The horse belongs to Prajāpati. / Directly he prospers it. / Whoever knows the attainment of the fire attains that desire for which desire the fire is piled. / When about to set out, he should attend upon the piled fire: 'By initiation I have attained you, by ascetic heat I have attained you, by the pressing [of soma] I have attained you, by the concluding bath I have attained you, by the barren cow I have attained you.' / That amounts to five. / The seasons are five. / He attains that desire for which desire the fire is piled. // 'There is a single brick,' say the theological disputants: speech is the single brick; the Brāhmaṇa is the single brick; these worlds are [the single brick]. / This indeed they used to say: 'We who are named Śarkarā know the piled fire as only three bricks, [namely] these worlds.' / The fire is to be piled with truth. / With 'bhūḥ' he should place the first perforated [brick]; with 'bhuvaḥ' the second; with 'svar' the third. / This is the truth of speech. / He piles the fire with truth. / The theological disputants say: 'Have you piled the fire with truth or without truth?' / He indeed piles the fire with truth who piles thus. / 'For which deity is the fire piled?' say the theological disputants. / 'For Prajāpati alone.' / 'What is his oblation?' / 'The self alone.'

अपां ह्य् एष कुलायः //
text_mt: This [universe] was in the beginning waters, fluid indeed. / Prajāpati, having become wind, was fluttering upon a lotus leaf. / He found no firm standing. / He saw this nest of the waters. / He brought it. / He set it down. / It became this [earth]. / Thence he stood firmly. / This [earth] indeed is the fire. / Therefore, when they dig into it, they dig down to the brick, down to gravel. / That which he placed in front became the head. / That is the eastern quarter. / That which he placed on the right became the right wing. / That is the southern quarter. / That which he placed behind became the tail. / That is the western quarter. / That which he placed on the left became the left wing. / That is the northern quarter. / That which he placed in the middle became the back. / That is the upward quarter. / This [earth] indeed is the fire consisting of five bricks. / Whoever knows thus is propagated. / He attains a firm standing. / The brāhmaṇa is indeed connected with Agni. / Therefore, to a brāhmaṇa it prospers in all quarters. / For he goes after his own quarter. / All this [earth] indeed blazes at night for birds to see. / Therefore birds do not settle on it at night. / This indeed is the nest of the waters. / Therefore the waters are liable to strike it down. / For this is the nest of the waters.

meaning:
यदि मन्येत पूर्वो मातिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्य इत्य् अष्टाव् उपदध्याल् लोकंपृणया पुरस्ताद् बहिष्पवमानस्यैकादश पुरस्तान् माध्यन्दिनस्य पवमानस्य द्वादश पुरस्ताद् आर्भवस्य पवमानस्य /
अयं वाव यः पवते स पवमानः /
वायुर् अग्नेस् तेजः /
य एवैनं पूर्वो ऽतिक्रान्तो भ्रातृव्यस् तं तेजसा प्रणुदते /
यदि मन्येत पश्चाद् इव भ्रातृव्य इति पश्चाद् उपदध्यात् स पवमानानाम् /
अयं वाव यः पवते स पवमानः /
वायुर् अग्नेस् तेजः /
य एवैनं पश्चाद् भ्रातृव्यस् तं तेजसापनुदते [ प्र श्रेयांसं ] भ्रातृव्यं नुदते प्रति पापीयांसं नुदते /
स एष सवनचित् /
प्रजापतिर् वा उख्यम् अग्निम् अबिभः /
तस्य शिरः प्रावर्तत /
तेन देवा अश्राम्यन् /
तस्यैतच् छिरः प्रत्यदधुर् यद् उखा /
तत् संवत्सरम् अरोहत् /
अग्निः प्रजापतिः /
यत् संवत्सरम् उख्यं बिभर्ति
प्रजापतेर् एव शिरः प्रतिदधाति /
तस्मात् संवत्सरम् उख्यो भर्तव्यः /
यद् अर्वाक् संवत्सराद् अरुश् चिद् एव सः //
येन देवा ज्योतिषोर्ध्वा उदायन् येनादित्या वसवो येन रुद्राः /
येनाङ्गिरसो महिमानम् आनशुस् तेनैतु यजमानः स्वस्ति //
इति घृतेनाक्त्वा समिधम् आदधाति /
समिद्धिर् एवैषा /
अथो यजमानस्यैवैतत् स्वस्त्ययनं क्रियते //
ये अग्नयः पुरीषिण आविष्टाः पृथिवीम् अनु /
तेषाम् असि त्वम् उत्तमः प्र नो जीवातवे सुव //
इति स्वम् अग्निं चितम् उपतिष्ठेत /
सर्वम् आयुर् एति /
उप त्वाग्ने दिवेदिव इत्य् एतेन त्र्यृचेनान्येषाम् /
आशिर् एव सा //
text_mt: If he should think, 'A rival has surpassed me previously,' he should place eight with the space-filling [brick] before the bahiṣpavamāna [stotra], eleven before the mādhyandina pavamāna, twelve before the ārbhava pavamāna. / This one who purifies himself is indeed the Pavamāna. / Vāyu is the brilliance of Agni. / Whatever rival has surpassed him previously, him he thrusts forth with brilliance. / If he should think, 'My rival is behind, as it were,' he should place [them] behind the pavamānas. / This one who purifies himself is indeed the Pavamāna. / Vāyu is the brilliance of Agni. / Whatever rival is behind him, him he thrusts away with brilliance. He thrusts forth a superior rival; he thrusts back an inferior one. / This is the savanacit [fire]. / Prajāpati bore the fire in the pot. / His head rolled away. / Over it the gods toiled. / They replaced this head of his, which is the pot. / It took a year to heal. / Agni is Prajāpati. / In that he bears the fire in the pot for a year, / he replaces the head of Prajāpati. / Therefore the fire in the pot is to be borne for a year. / If [it is for] less than a year, it is indeed a wound. / 'By which light the gods ascended upward, by which the Ādityas, the Vasus, by which the Rudras, / by which the Aṅgirases attained greatness, by that may the sacrificer go to welfare'— / having anointed with ghee, he places the kindling-stick with this [verse]. / This is indeed rekindling. / And this is made a means of welfare for the sacrificer. / 'Which fires, rich in earth, have entered along the earth, / of them you are the highest; impel us to life'— / with this [verse] he should attend upon his own piled fire. / He goes to a full life. / With this triplet, 'To you, O Agni, day by day,' [he attends upon the piled fire] of others. / It is indeed a blessing.

text_mt: When the hearths are placed, then he should place three [bricks] with three [formulas] to Bṛhaspati on the south. / Then three with three to Yama, then three with three to Rudra, then three with three to Varuṇa. / From the south the demons wished to strike the sacrifice of the gods. / The [bricks] to Bṛhaspati struck them away. / In that [the bricks] to Bṛhaspati are placed on the south, / [it is] for the smiting away of the demons. / Then [those] to Yama. / By these indeed these worlds shone near and far for Asita Devala. / For him for whom these are placed, these worlds shine near and far alike. / Then [those] to Rudra. / Agni is Rudra. / He is liable to arise after this [man] from here and slay [him]. / In that [he places the bricks] to Rudra, / he appeases Rudra. / Then [those] to Varuṇa. / The waters are Varuṇa. / Varuṇa is liable to come out after this [man] from the final bath and seize [him]. / In that [he places the bricks] to Varuṇa, / he appeases Varuṇa. / If while [the fire] is being borne in the pot this god should menace the creatures, he should place three [kindling-sticks] with three healing gāyatrī verses to Agni. / He indeed menaces the creatures at that time. / In that he places [them] with the healing [verses], / he applies a remedy. / If while [the fire] is being borne in the pot he should desire, 'May it rain,' he should place three kindling-sticks with three verses to Sūrya that contain [the word] ray. / That Āditya indeed afflicts the creatures with heat at that time when [Parjanya does not rain...]

तस्य ते पवित्रपते पवित्रेणेति /
यज्ञो वै पवित्रपतिः /
यज्ञायैवैतत् पुनीते /
यस्मै कं पुने तच् छकेयम् इति /
यज्ञं श्केयम् इत्य् एवैतद् आह /
अन्वञ्चं पावयति /
अन्वङ् वै पुरुषं प्राणः /
यदा वै प्राणस् तिर्यङ् भवत्य् अथ प्रमीयते /
यत् तिर्यञ्चम् अस्य प्राणं कुर्यात् प्रमीयेत /
अन्वात्मम् एवास्य प्राणं करोति /
बहिष्पावयति /
मनुष्यलोक एवैनं पावयित्वा पूतं देवलोकं प्रणयति //
text_mt:
The initiated is an oblation.
An oblation not anointed with butter does not attain sacrificial fitness.
When he anoints him,
he indeed places butter upon him
for sacrificial fitness.
Ghee belongs to the gods, boiled butter to men, clarified butter to the Gandharvas, naturally melted butter to Āditya.
Fresh butter is neither among the gods nor among men.
He who is initiated is neither among the gods nor among men, having departed from this world.
When he anoints him with fresh butter,
[it is] for prosperity.
He puts on a garment.
The hem belongs to Agni, the tuck to the Fathers, the border to the plants, the wind-protecting fringe to Vāyu, the warps and the wefts to the All-Gods, the interstices to the asterisms.
The garment belongs to all the deities.
The initiated belongs to all the deities.
He enriches him with all the deities.
He anoints his eyes.
When Indra had slain [Vṛtra], the demons pursued him.
He blocked them out with the ointment-mountain.
The demons pursue him who is initiated,
for so it happens.
When he anoints his eyes,
[it is] for shutting out the demons.
Indra slew Vṛtra.
His eye flew away.
It entered Mount Trikakubh.
When he anoints his eyes,
[it is] for securing that very eye.
Twice he anoints the right eye, once the left.
The sacrifice is threefold.
At the very front he takes hold of the sacrifice.
Three times he anoints the right eye, twice the left.
The sacrifice is fivefold.
He secures the sacrifice.
He anoints the right eye first.
Men indeed anoint the left first.
[It is] for distinction.
He anoints with a yajus-formula.
Men indeed anoint without a yajus-formula.
[It is] for distinction.
He anoints outward, he does not run back over it.
Men indeed anoint back and forth.
[It is] for distinction.
He anoints with a reed-stalk.
Men indeed anoint with a porcupine quill.
[It is] for distinction.
It has a tuft.
That which has a tuft belongs to Mitra; that which is shed belongs to Varuṇa.
The initiated belongs to Mitra.
[It is] for prosperity.
Deficient, as it were, defective, as it were, is the eye.
When he anoints his eyes,
he fills that very [deficiency],
for freedom from defect.
He purifies him.
Indra slew Vṛtra.
He struck him right in the waters.
Those [parts] of them that were sacrificial, fit for sacrifice, stepped forth.
They became the plants.
The brilliance that was theirs became darbha-grass.
Therefore they are a strainer.
Therefore with darbha-grass they purify the waters.
When he purifies him with darbha-shoots,
he purifies him with the very brilliance of the waters.
He purifies him with two.
Two are truth and untruth.
With truth indeed he purifies his untruth.
Two are the in-breath and the out-breath.
He purifies him with three.
[Three indeed are] the vital breaths: in-breath, diffused breath, out-breath.
These very ones he places in the sacrificer.
He purifies him with five.
The human being is fivefold.
As great as his body is, that much he purifies.
[He purifies him with seven.]
[Seven indeed are the meters.]
[With the meters indeed he purifies him.]
[He purifies him with nine.]
Nine indeed are the vital breaths.
With the vital breaths indeed he purifies him.
He purifies him with twenty-one.
The human being is twenty-one-fold: ten fingers of the hands, ten toes of the feet, the trunk as the twenty-first.
As great as his body is, that much he purifies.
'May the lord of thought purify you,' [he says].
The brahman indeed is the lord of thought.
With the brahman indeed he purifies him.
'May the lord of speech purify you,' [he says].
He indeed is the purifier.
'May the divine Savitṛ purify you,' [he says].
Impelled by Savitṛ he purifies him with the deities.
'With an unbroken strainer,' [he says].
Without a hitch he thus purifies [him].
'With the rays of Sūrya,' [he says].
With the very body of Āditya he purifies him.
'With your strainer, O lord of the strainer,' [he says].
The sacrifice indeed is the lord of the strainer.
For the sacrifice he thus purifies [him].
'For whatever purpose I purify myself, may I be capable of that,' [he says].
'May I be capable of the sacrifice,' he thus says.
He purifies him lengthwise.
Lengthwise indeed along the human being goes the vital breath.
When the vital breath goes crosswise, then he perishes.
If he were to make his vital breath go crosswise, he would perish.
Along his body he makes his vital breath [go].
He purifies him outside.
Having purified him in the world of men, he leads him purified to the world of the gods.

meaning:
गर्भो दीक्षितो योनिर् दीक्षितविमितम् उल्बं दीक्षितवसनं जरायुं कृष्णाजिनम् /
एतस्माद् वै योनेर् इन्द्रो ऽजायत /
कुलायम् एवैतद् आसीवनं कृत्वोपचरति /
तस्माद् दीक्षितम् / नान्यत्र दीक्षितविमितात् सूर्यो ऽभिनिम्रोचेन् नान्यत्राभ्युदियात् /
स्वाद् एव योनेः प्रजायते /
आकूत्यै प्रयुजे ऽग्नये स्वाहेति /
आकूय वै यज्ञः प्रयुज्यते /
यत्रैव यज्ञम् आकुवते तद् एनम् आलभते /
मेधायै मनसे ऽग्नये स्वाहेति /
मेधया वै मनसाभिगच्छति यजतां स्य इति /
यज्ञम् एवावरुन्द्धे /
दीक्षायै तपस ऽग्नये स्वाहेति /
दीक्षया वै तपसा यज्ञं प्राप्नोति /
यज्ञम् एवावरुन्द्धे /
सरस्वत्यै पूष्णे ऽग्नये स्वाहेति /
वाग् वै सरस्वती पशवः पूषा /
वाचा पशुभ्यो ऽधि यज्ञम् आलभते /
आपो देवीर् बृहतीर् विश्वशम्भुव इति /
आपो वै यज्ञः /
दिवि यज्ञो ऽन्तरिक्षे पृथिव्याम् /
ब्रह्म बृहस्पतिः /
अत्रात्र वै यज्ञः /
यत्रयत्रैव यज्ञस् तत एनं ब्रह्मणालभते /
पञ्चैतानि जुहोति /
पाङ्क्तो यज्ञः /
यज्ञम् एवावरुन्द्धे /
यज्ञस्य वा एते संभारा यद् एतानि यजूंसि /
यद् एतानि न जुहुयाद् असंभृतो ऽस्य यज्ञः स्यात् /
यद् एतानि जुहोति यावान् एव यज्ञस् तं संभरति /
अदीक्षितो वा एकयाहुत्या /
अदन्ति ह स्म वा एतस्य पुरान्नं यस्यैतानि न हूयन्ते /
यद् एतानि [ जुहोति ] दीक्षितत्वायैव द्वितीयत्वायैव /
अग्नये स्वाहाग्नये स्वाहेति जुहोति /
अग्निः सर्वा देवताः /
सर्वा एव देवता अवरुन्द्धे /
पञ्चैतानि जुहोति /
औद्ग्रहणं षष्ठम् /
षड् ऋतवः /
ऋतुष्व् एव प्रतितिष्ठति /
यज्ञः सृष्टः प्र यजुर् अव्लिनात् प्र साम /
तम् ऋग् एवायच्छन् नव सामानि द्वादश यजूंषि /
तस्मान् नवभिर् बहिष्पवमानं स्तुवन्ति /
ऋचौद्ग्रहणं जुह्वति /
यद् ऋचौद्ग्रहणं जुहोति
यज्ञम् एव सृष्टं प्रत्युद्दृचा यच्छति /
द्वादशभिर् ह स्म वै पुरा कारुद्वेषिण औद्ग्रहणं जुह्वति /
एतद् एव द्वादशगृहीतं कृत्वा जुहुयात् /
तेनैव तद् आप्नोति /
पूर्णया स्रुचा जुहोति /
पूर्णः प्रजापतिः /
प्रजापतिम् एवाप्नोति /
यद् ऊनया जुहुयाद् भ्रातृव्याय लोकं कुर्यात् /
कामार्तं वै पूर्णम् /
यं हि कामं कामयते तं पूर्णस्य कुरुते /
यम् एव कामं कामयते तम् अवरुन्द्धे //
स्वे छन्दसि यज्ञः प्रतिष्ठाप्यः /
अनुष्टुब् वै प्रजापतेः स्वं छन्दः /
यज्ञः प्रजापतिः /
यद् अनुष्टुभौद्ग्रहणं जुहोति
स्व एव च्छन्दसि यज्ञं प्रतिष्ठापयते /
छन्दःप्रतिष्ठानो वै यज्ञः /
स यथाछन्दसं छन्दःसु प्रतिष्ठाप्यः /
सैषानुष्टुप् /
तस्याः सप्ताक्षरम् एकं पदम् अष्टाक्षराणि त्रीणि /
तेषां सप्तानां यानि त्रीणि तान्य् अष्टाव् उपयन्ति /
तान्य् एकादश /
सा त्रिष्टुप् /
यानि चत्वारि तान्य् अष्टाव् उपयन्ति /
तानि द्वादश /
सा जगती /
यान्य् अष्टौ सा गायत्री /
अविभक्तानुष्टुप् /
स्वाहाकारेण पङ्क्तिः /
एतावन्ति वै छन्दांसि /
यज्ञम् एव यथाछन्दसं छन्दःसु प्रतिष्ठापयते //
यज्ञः सृष्टो देवताभिरालभ्यः /
विश्वो देवस्य नेतुर् इति
यन् नेतृमती तेन सावित्री /
मर्त इति
पितृदेवत्या /
विश्व इति
वैश्वदेवी /
द्युम्नम् इति
बार्हस्पत्या /
पुष्यत्व् इति
पौष्णी /
सारस्वतः स्वाहाकारः /
एतावतीर् वै देवताः /
यज्ञम् एवैतत् सृष्टं देवताभिर् आलभते /
यज्ञश् च सृष्टो हुतस् त्रेधा प्रावि[शद् ऋचं तृतीयेन साम तृतीयेन यजुस् तृतीयेन / ... // ]
text_mt: The initiated is an embryo, the shed of the initiated is the womb, the garment of the initiated is the amnion, the black antelope skin is the chorion. / From this womb Indra was born. / Having made a nest, as it were, a sewing, he approaches it. / Therefore the sun should not set upon the initiated nor rise upon him anywhere other than the shed of the initiated. / He is born from his own womb. / 'To intention, to impulse, to Agni, svāhā!' / Having intended, the sacrifice is set in motion. / Where indeed they intend the sacrifice, there he takes hold of it. / 'To wisdom, to mind, to Agni, svāhā!' / Through wisdom, through mind, he considers: 'Let them sacrifice [saying] "I am".' / He secures the sacrifice. / 'To consecration, to austerity, to Agni, svāhā!' / Through consecration, through austerity, he attains the sacrifice. / He secures the sacrifice. / 'To Sarasvatī, to Pūṣan, to Agni, svāhā!' / Speech is Sarasvatī, cattle are Pūṣan. / Through speech he takes hold of the sacrifice from cattle. / 'O divine waters, great, all-beneficent!' / The waters are the sacrifice. / In heaven is the sacrifice, in the intermediate space, on earth. / Bṛhaspati is the sacred word. / Here and here indeed is the sacrifice. / Wherever the sacrifice is, from there he takes hold of it by means of the sacred word. / He offers these five. / The sacrifice is fivefold. / He secures the sacrifice. / These yajus-formulas are the requisites of the sacrifice. / If he should not offer these, his sacrifice would be unequipped. / Since he offers these, he equips the sacrifice as great as it is. / By one oblation one is not initiated. / Formerly indeed they used to eat the food of him for whom these are not offered. / In that he offers these, [it is] for the state of being initiated, for duality. / 'To Agni svāhā! To Agni svāhā!' he offers. / Agni is all the deities. / He secures all the deities. / He offers these five. / The elevation [libation] is the sixth. / Six are the seasons. / He firmly establishes [himself] in the seasons. / When the sacrifice was created, the yajus collapsed, the sāman collapsed. / The ṛc alone held it fast—nine sāmans, twelve yajuses. / Therefore they praise the out-of-doors pavamāna with nine [verses]. / They offer the elevation [libation] with an ṛc. / In that he offers the elevation [libation] with an ṛc, / he holds fast the created sacrifice with a final verse. / Formerly indeed the Kārudveṣins used to offer the elevation [libation] with twelve. / Having made it taken twelve times, he should offer it. / Thereby he attains that. / He offers with a full ladle. / Prajāpati is full. / He attains Prajāpati. / If he should offer with a deficient [ladle], he would make room for his rival. / The full is for the fulfillment of desire. / For whatever desire he desires, that he accomplishes with the full. / Whatever desire he desires, that he secures. // The sacrifice is to be established in its own meter. / The anuṣṭubh is Prajāpati's own meter. / The sacrifice is Prajāpati. / In that he offers the elevation [libation] with an anuṣṭubh, / he establishes the sacrifice in its own meter. / The sacrifice is supported by meters. / It is to be established in the meters according to each meter. / This is the anuṣṭubh. / Of it, one quarter has seven syllables, three have eight syllables. / Of those seven, those which are three join the eight. / They are eleven. / That is the triṣṭubh. / Those which are four join the eight. / They are twelve. / That is the jagatī. / Those which are eight, that is the gāyatrī. / The undivided is the anuṣṭubh. / With the utterance of svāhā it is the paṅkti. / So many indeed are the meters. / He establishes the sacrifice in the meters according to each meter. // The sacrifice, when created, is to be taken hold of by the deities. / 'Of the god, the leader of all...': / in that it contains 'leader', thereby it belongs to Savitṛ. / 'Mortal...': / it belongs to the Fathers as deity. / 'All...': / it belongs to the All-Gods. / 'Splendor...': / it belongs to Bṛhaspati. / 'May he foster...': / it belongs to Pūṣan. / The utterance of svāhā belongs to Sarasvatī. / So many indeed are the deities. / He takes hold of this created sacrifice with the deities. / And the sacrifice, when created and offered, entered threefold: [into the ṛc with a third, into the sāman with a third, into the yajus with a third. ... //]

meaning:
... [ यद्य् एकं स्यात् पा]दं प्रतिषीव्येत् /
अनन्तर्हितो यजमानो यज्ञाच् च देवताभ्यश् च भवत्य् अनन्तर्हितो यज्ञो देवताभ्यः /
विष्णोः शर्मासि शर्म यजमानस्येति /
विष्णुर् वै यज्ञः वैष्णवो यजमानः /
विष्णुनैव यज्ञेनात्मानम् उभयतः सयुजं कुरुते /
यज्ञो यद् असृज्यत तस्योल्बम् अन्ववेष्टत /
तद् दीक्षितवसनम् अभवत् /
गर्भो दीक्षितः /
यद् दीक्षितवसनं परिधत्ते
स्वेनैव योनिनात्मानम् ओर्णुते /
तस्मान् महत् कार्यम् /
एवम् इव ह्य् उल्बेन गर्भ आवृत इव च्छन्न इव /
न प्रत्यक्षं वदेत् /
वाचो ऽयातयामत्वाय //
text_mt: ... [If it should be one,] he should sew on a border. / The sacrificer is not separated from the sacrifice and from the deities, and the sacrifice is not separated from the deities. / 'You are the shelter of Viṣṇu, the shelter of the sacrificer.' / Viṣṇu is the sacrifice; the sacrificer belongs to Viṣṇu. / Through Viṣṇu, through the sacrifice, he makes himself united on both sides. / When the sacrifice was created, its amnion wrapped around it. / That became the garment of the initiated. / The initiated is an embryo. / In that he puts on the garment of the initiated, / he covers himself with his own womb. / Therefore it must be made large. / For thus the embryo is covered, as it were, veiled, as it were, by the amnion. / He should not speak directly, / so that speech does not become stale.

meaning:
अङ्गिरसो वै स्वर्गं लोकं यन्तस् ते मेखलाः संन्यकिरन् /
ततः शर उदतिष्ठत् /
यच् छरमयी मेखला भवति
ताम् एव मेखलाम् आलभते /
देवा वै यत्रोर्जं व्यभजन्त ततः शर उदतिष्ठत् /
यच् छरमयी मेखला भवति
ताम् एवोर्जम् आलभते /
ऊर्ग् वै मेखला /
मध्यं प्रति परिव्ययति /
ऊर्जम् एव मध्यतो दधाति यजमानेषु च प्रजासु च /
तस्मान् मध्यतः प्रजा ऊर्ग् ऊर्जयति /
नाभिं प्रति परिव्ययति /
ऊर्ध्वं वै पुरुषस्य नाभ्या मेध्यम् अवाचीनम् अमेध्यम् /
मेध्यस्य चामेध्यस्य च व्यावृत्त्यै /
त्रिवृद् भवति /
त्रिवृता वै स्तोमेन प्रजापतिः प्रजा असृजत /
त्रिवृद् वज्रः
वज्रम् एव भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति /
इन्द्रो वै वृत्राय वज्रं प्राहरत् /
तस्य यत् प्राशीर्यत स शरो ऽभवत् /
तच् छरस्य शरत्वम् /
वज्रो वै शरः /
यच् छरमयी मेखला भवति
वज्रम् एव भ्रातृव्याय प्रहरति /
यं द्विष्यात् तं परिव्ययन् ध्यायेत् /
वज्रेणैवैनं समर्पयति /
मेखला पुंसो भवति योक्त्रं स्त्रियाः /
स्त्री वै मेखला पुमान् योक्त्रम् /
मिथुनम् एव यज्ञमुखे विपर्यूहति
प्रजननाय /
वज्रो वै मेखला /
क्षुद् उदरं पाप्मा भ्रातृव्यः /
यन् मेखलां परिव्ययते
वज्रेणैव पाप्मानं भ्रातृव्यम् अपहते //
यज्ञो वै देवेष्व् आसीद् दक्षिणा पितृषु /
स यज्ञो दक्षिणाम् अभ्यकामयत /
तं पितरो ऽब्रुवन् देवेषु णो भागधेयम् इच्छेति /
ते ऽब्रुवंस् तृतीयसवनभागा असन्न् इति /
तस्मात् पितृभ्यस् तृतीयसवनं क्रियते /
तम् अह्वयत् /
तां हूतो ऽधावत् /
तस्मात् पुमान् स्त्रीहूतो धावति /
तस्माच् छ्रोत्रिय स्त्रीकामतमः /
स हि यज्ञस्य नेदिष्ठी /
तां समभवत् /
तद् इन्द्रो ऽचायत् /
सो ऽमन्यत यो वा इतो जनिष्यते स एवेदं भविष्यतीति /
तं योनिं प्राविशत् /
तस्माद् अजायत /
स पुनः प्रत्यवैक्षत /
सो ऽमन्यत यो वा इतो ऽपरो जनिष्यते स मे भ्रातृव्यो भविष्यतीति /
तम् अववृज्य प्राच्छिनत् /
सा विषाणाभवत् /
यद् विषाणा भवति
यज्ञस्यैव रेत इन्द्रस्य योनिं दक्षिणाया योनिम् आलभते /
पञ्चावृद् भवति /
पञ्चभिर् हि स तां निवेष्ट्याच्छिनत् /
इन्द्रस्य योनिर् असीति / इन्द्रस्य ह्य् एषा योनिः /
कृष्यै त्वा सुसस्याया इति /
तस्मात् कृष्टं पच्यते /
उत्कृधीति /
तस्माद् ऊर्ध्वा ओषधय उत्पद्यन्ते /
यजुषा कण्डूयते /
अयजुषा हि मनुष्याः कण्डूयन्ते /
व्यावृत्त्यै /
यद् अयजुषा कण्डूयेत वरुणवत् कण्डूयेत /
अपि गर्भाः पामना जायेरन् //
वाग् वै देवान् मनुष्यान् प्रविशन्त्यैत् /
तस्या यद् अत्यरिच्यत तद् वनस्पतीन् प्राविशत् /
सैषा वनस्पतिषु वाग् वदति या दुन्दुभौ या नाड्यां या तूणवे /
यद् दण्डस् /
वाच एवातिरिक्तम् अवरुन्द्धे /
तं मैत्रावरुणाय प्रयच्छति /
वाचम् एवास्मै तत् प्रयच्छति /
तां शश्वद् ऋत्विग्भ्यो विभजति /
तस्माद् अस्य वाङ् नोपदस्यति /
आस्यदघ्नः कार्यः /
तावती हीयं वाग् वदति /
अथो एतावती वाचा वीर्यं क्रियते /
यो वृक्षः फलग्रहिस् तस्य कुर्यात् फलग्रहिर् असानीति //
text_mt: The Aṅgirases were going to the heavenly world; they scattered off their girdles. / From that the reed arose. / In that the girdle is made of reed, / he takes hold of that very girdle. / Where the gods distributed vigor, from that the reed arose. / In that the girdle is made of reed, / he takes hold of that very vigor. / The girdle is vigor. / He girds it around the middle. / He places vigor right in the middle, in the sacrificers and in offspring. / Therefore vigor invigorates offspring from the middle. / He girds it around the navel. / The part of a man above the navel is fit for sacrifice; what is below is unfit for sacrifice. / [It is] for the separation of the fit for sacrifice and the unfit for sacrifice. / It is threefold. / By means of the threefold stoma, Prajāpati created offspring. / The thunderbolt is threefold. / He hurls the thunderbolt at his rival. / Indra hurled the thunderbolt at Vṛtra. / That part of it which shattered became reed (śara). / That is the reed-nature (śaratva) of the reed. / The reed is indeed a thunderbolt. / In that the girdle is made of reed, / he hurls the thunderbolt at his rival. / Whomever he hates, him he should contemplate while girding. / He strikes him with the thunderbolt itself. / There is a girdle for the man, a yoke-halter for the woman. / The girdle is a female, the yoke-halter a male. / He transposes the pair at the opening of the sacrifice / for procreation. / The girdle is a thunderbolt. / Hunger is the belly; evil is the rival. / When he girds the girdle, / with the thunderbolt he strikes away the evil rival. // The sacrifice was among the gods, the sacrificial fee among the Fathers. / That sacrifice desired the sacrificial fee. / The Fathers said to him: 'Seek a share for us among the gods.' / They said: 'Let them be sharing in the third pressing.' / Therefore the third pressing is performed for the Fathers. / He called to her. / Being called, he ran to her. / Therefore a man, called by a woman, runs. / Therefore a learned person is most desirous of women, / for he is nearest to the sacrifice. / He united with her. / Indra perceived that. / He thought: 'Whoever will be born from here, he alone will become this [all].' / He entered that womb. / He was born from it. / He looked back again. / He thought: 'Whoever else will be born from here, he will be my rival.' / Having twisted it off, he tore it away. / That became the horn. / In that there is a horn, / he takes hold of the semen of the sacrifice, the womb of Indra, the womb of the sacrificial fee. / It is fivefold. / For having wrapped it around with five [coils], he tore it off. / 'You are the womb of Indra.' For this is the womb of Indra. / 'For plowing, for good crops.' / Therefore what is plowed ripens. / 'Rise up!' / Therefore plants arise standing upright. / He scratches himself with a formula. / For men scratch themselves without a formula. / [It is] for distinction. / If he were to scratch without a formula, he would scratch like Varuṇa. / Even the embryos would be born with itch. // Speech went entering the gods and men. / What remained over of it entered the trees. / That is this speech that speaks in trees: that which is in the drum, in the reed-flute, in the lute. / In that there is a staff, / he wins the surplus of speech. / He gives it to the Maitrāvaruṇa. / He gives speech to him. / He continually distributes it among the priests. / Therefore his speech does not fail. / It should be made reaching to the mouth. / For just so far does this speech speak. / Moreover, with so much speech is manly strength exerted. / He should make it of a tree that bears fruit, [thinking:] 'May I be fruit-bearing!'

meaning:
स्वाहा यज्ञं मनस इति /
मनसा वै यज्ञ आलभ्यते /
वातयोनिर् यज्ञः /
दिवि यज्ञो ऽन्तरिक्षे पृथिव्याम् /
अत्रात्र वै यज्ञः /
यत्रयत्रैव यज्ञस् तत एनं मनसालभते /
तं यत्वास्ते /
यज्ञम् एव तद् यत्वास्ते /
यद् विसृजेद् यज्ञं विसृजेत् /
यदि विसृजेत् पुनर् दीक्षयेत् /
यत् पुनर् दीक्षयेद् आहुतीर् अतिरेचयेत् /
गायत्रीं वैष्णवीम् अनुब्रूयात् /
वाग् वै गायत्री यज्ञो विष्णुः /
वाचैव यज्ञं संतनोति /
बार्हस्पत्याम् उत्तराम् अनुब्रूयात् /
ब्रह्म वै बृहस्पतिः /
ब्रह्मणा यज्ञस्यार्तं निष्क्रियते /
ब्रह्मणैव यज्ञस्यार्तं निष्करोति /
त्वम् अग्ने व्रतपा असीत्य् अग्नये व्रतपतये ऽनुब्रूयात् /
व्रतपतिं वा एतस्य व्रतं गच्छति यो दीक्षितः सन्न व्रतं चरति /
अग्निर् देवानां व्रतपतिः /
व्रतपतेर् एवाधि व्रतम् आलभते /
अदीक्षिष्टायम् असाव् आमुष्यायण इति त्रिर् उपांश्व् आह त्रिर् उच्चैः /
देवेभ्यश् चैव मनुष्येभ्यश् च यज्ञं प्राह /
नक्षत्रं दृष्ट्वा वाचं विसृजते /
दि[वा वै मनुष्या यज्ञेन चरन्ति नक्तं देवाः / ... // ]
text_mt: 'Svāhā, to the sacrifice, from the mind!' / By the mind indeed the sacrifice is grasped. / The sacrifice has wind as its source. / The sacrifice is in heaven, in the intermediate space, on earth. / Right here and there is the sacrifice. / Wherever the sacrifice is, from there he grasps it with the mind. / Having restrained [speech], he sits. / Having restrained the sacrifice, he sits. / If he should release [it], he would release the sacrifice. / If he should release [it], he should cause him to be initiated again. / If he were to cause him to be initiated again, he would make the oblations redundant. / He should recite a gāyatrī verse to Viṣṇu. / The gāyatrī is speech; Viṣṇu is the sacrifice. / With speech he stretches out the sacrifice. / He should recite a subsequent one to Bṛhaspati. / Bṛhaspati is the brahman. / By means of the brahman what is afflicted of the sacrifice is repaired. / With the brahman he repairs what is afflicted of the sacrifice. / 'You, O Agni, are the guardian of vows'—[with this] he should recite to Agni, guardian of vows. / The vow of him who, being initiated, does not observe the vow goes to the lord of vows. / Agni is the lord of vows of the gods. / From the lord of vows he takes hold of the vow. / 'This N.N., son of N.N., has been initiated'—he says thrice in a low voice, thrice aloud. / He announces the sacrifice to the gods and to men. / Having seen a star, he releases speech. / [By day men perform the sacrifice, by night the gods. ... //]

meaning:
देवाश् च वा असुराश् च समावद् एव यज्ञे ऽकुर्वत /
यद् एव देवा अकुर्वत तद् असुरा अकुर्वत /
अग्निहोत्रं दर्शपौर्णमासौ चातुर्मास्यान्य् एष वाव तर्हि यज्ञ आसीत् /

तस्माद् याग्निहोत्रस्य स्कन्नस्य प्रायश्चित्तिः सा व्रतस्य स्कन्नस्य प्रायश्चित्तिः /
तस्माद् द्विव्रतो दीक्षितः स्यात् /
द्विर् ह्य् अग्निहोत्रं जुह्वति /
तेषां यत् पौस्र्णमासम् आसीत् तम् अग्नीषोमीयं पशुम् अकुर्वत यः पूर्वेद्युर् आलभ्यते /
यद् दार्शं तम् आग्नेयं यो ऽनुसवनम् आलभ्यते /
वैश्वदेवम् एव प्रातःसवनम् अकुर्वत वरुणप्रधासान् माध्यन्दिनं सवनं साकमेधांस् तृतीयसवनम् /
तृतीयसवने पितृयज्ञम् अवाकल्पयंस् तृतीयसवने त्र्यम्बकान् /
ते ऽसुरा अपक्रामन्तो अब्रुवन् न वा इमे ध्वर्तवा अभवन्न् इति /
तद् अध्वरस्याध्वरत्वम् /
ततो देवा अभवन् परासुरा अभवन् /
य एवं विद्वान् दीक्षते यम् एवं विद्वान् दीक्षयति भवत्य् आत्मना परास्य भ्रातृव्यो भवति //
text_mt: The gods and the Asuras performed alike in the sacrifice. / Whatever the gods did, that the Asuras did. / The Agnihotra, the new- and full-moon sacrifices, and the four-month sacrifices—just this was the sacrifice then. / The gods saw this Soma-sacrifice. / They brought it. / They initiated [the sacrificer]. / They made the Agnihotra itself the vow-food. / The Agnihotra is indeed the vow-food. / Therefore, whatever is the expiation for spilled Agnihotra, that is the expiation for spilled vow-food. / Therefore, the initiated one should have two vow-meals. / For twice they offer the Agnihotra. / What was their full-moon sacrifice, that they made the animal for Agni and Soma, which is seized on the previous day. / What was the new-moon sacrifice, that [they made] the animal for Agni, which is seized at the pressing. / They made the Vaiśvadeva the morning pressing, the Varuṇapradhāsa the midday pressing, the Sākamedha the third pressing. / At the third pressing they arranged the Pitṛyajña; at the third pressing, the Tryambakas. / Those Asuras, stepping away, said: 'These have become not to be harmed.' / That is why the sacrifice is called adhvara. / Then the gods flourished, the Asuras perished. / He who, knowing thus, is initiated, or whom, knowing thus, one initiates, prospers in himself, and his rival perishes.

text_mt: To the heavenly world indeed they go forth by this, namely the introductory [offering]. / That is why the introductory offering is called prāyaṇīya. / He is indeed cut off from this world who goes to that world. / In that the concluding [offering] belongs to Aditi, he firmly establishes himself in this very world. / The gods, having slain the Asuras and fleeing from blood-money, confused the quarters [thinking], 'Lest [another should recognize this after us.' / As to that, they say: 'The Sādhyas were gods prior to the gods. / Having confused the quarters, they went to the heavenly world, lest] another should recognize this world after us.' / These latter gods sought to recognize them. / They did not recognize them. / Aditi said: 'Let me choose a boon: the sacrifice shall have its beginning in me and its conclusion in me.' / Therefore the introductory offering belongs to Aditi, and the concluding offering belongs to Aditi. / For her boon was chosen. / 'Sacrifice to Pathyā Svasti,' she said, 'by her you will recognize the eastern quarter.' / 'Sacrifice to Agni,' she said, 'by him the southern [quarter].' / 'Sacrifice to Soma,' she said, 'by him the western [quarter].' / 'Sacrifice to Savitṛ,' she said, 'by him the northern [quarter].' / 'I myself [am] these two,' she said. [...]

text_mt: [...] with speech alone they go forth, with speech they conclude. / The introductory offering belongs to Aditi, the concluding offering belongs to Aditi. / In both this world and that world he firmly establishes himself by means of the face of the sacrifice. / The quarters are indeed the heavenly world. / The quarters have these deities. / In that he sacrifices with the introductory offering, / he steps onto the quarters, the heavenly world. / Just as a mat is woven, so the sacrifice is woven. / In that the introductory offering belongs to Aditi, and the concluding offering belongs to Aditi, / he ties these two borders at the ends, / for firmness, to prevent slipping away. / What are the invitatory verses of the introductory offering are the offering verses of the concluding offering; what are the offering verses are the invitatory verses. / With that very [verse] by which they go forth, with that they conclude, / for continuity of procedure, for continuous recognition. / He should interweave the invitatory and offering verses for him whom he hates. / He makes him fall away from this world and he does not reach that world. / Just as one strays from the path, such is that. / He cuts him off from both sides. / The introductory offering should be without after-offerings; the concluding offering without fore-offerings. / For this oblation is the same, / for continuity. / The fore-offerings are the self, the after-offerings are offspring. / If he were to do so, he would separate himself from both himself and offspring; he would die without offspring. / They should both have fore-offerings and after-offerings. / The oblation is the same, the deity is the same, the stirring-stick is the same. / Thereby he maintains the continuity of the sacrifice. / He does not separate himself from either the self or offspring. / They discuss: 'Should it be concluded, or should it not be concluded?' / The sacrifice indeed flows away when not concluded. / Following that flowing [sacrifice], the sacrificer flows away with offspring and cattle. / It is certainly to be concluded. / But he should not cause the wife to sacrifice together. / For she is unfit for sacrifice, unpurified, unable to go to the heavenly world. / He causes her to sacrifice together at the concluding offering. / Just as a traveler comes to his own home, in this very way the sacrificer firmly establishes himself upon this world with his wife. / For sacrificers eat food of the initiated, and yet they do not become better off. / He is initiated then when he sacrifices with the introductory offering. / He is initiated now when he arises from the final bath. / Upon the remnants of the introductory offering he pours out the concluding offering. / He should not eat of the concluding offering alone. / He avoids the food of the initiated. / He becomes better off.
